finding.issue: The constructor takes const Trajectory& and const vector<PhaseSpan>& and stores them as reference members (lines 62-70). A value-looking 'Input' struct can therefore silently dangle when built from temporaries; binding a temporary to a reference member does not extend its lifetime. The comment at :57-58 says 'borrowed only for evaluateFlight()', but nothing prevents `FlightEvaluationInput in{makeTraj(), {{T, PhaseKind::CRUISE, "x"}}};`.
finding.misreading_example: A user writes `FlightEvaluationInput input{traj, {{traj.getTotalDuration(), PhaseKind::CRUISE, "flight"}}};` (brace-init spans, as in the doc's style) and then calls evaluateFlight(input) on the next line. input.phases now refers to a destroyed vector, which is undefined behaviour.
finding.reason: The name is acceptable; the API shape invites misuse. Options: add deleted rvalue-reference constructor overloads, or state the 'must outlive' rule on the constructor itself. No rename needed.
finding.affected_callers: FlightEvaluationInput: 6 code references / 4 files (flight_evaluator.h/.cpp, flight_evaluator_example.cpp:18, segment_chain_planner.cpp:3255); 8 references in 1 test file. All current callers pass named lvalues.

verdict.evidence: flight_evaluator.h:62-65: the constructor `FlightEvaluationInput(const poly_traj::Trajectory &flight, const std::vector<PhaseSpan> &spans) : trajectory(flight), phases(spans)` stores its arguments in reference members `const poly_traj::Trajectory &trajectory;` (:69) and `const std::vector<PhaseSpan> &phases;` (:70). Both parameters are const&, so a prvalue binds to them, and with brace-init `{traj, {{T, PhaseKind::CRUISE, "x"}}}` that prvalue is a temporary vector. The temporary is destroyed at the end of the declaration's full-expression. No rvalue overload is deleted, so this compiles without a diagnostic. PhaseSpan (flight_evaluation.h:22-26) is an aggregate, so the nested brace form in the misreading example is valid syntax. The comment at :57-58, "References/pointers are borrowed only for evaluateFlight()", says what the data is used for. It does not say the argument objects must outlive the `input` object, and it sits on the struct, not on the constructor. It does not settle the issue. `const std::vector<size_t> *piece_leg` (:75) has the same borrowing, but it is a raw pointer and visibly non-owning. The report side is fine: FlightEvaluationReport owns `std::vector<PhaseSpan> phases` (:173), and docs/design/planning_computation_usage_ko.md:175 states the report survives after the inputs are gone. So the hazard is limited to the window between constructing the input and calling evaluateFlight. evaluateFlight is defined at flight_evaluator.cpp:66 and takes `const FlightEvaluationInput &`.
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/docs/design/planning_computation_usage_ko.md:162 `FlightEvaluationInput input(flight, phases);` (doc snippet, named local at :159-160)
verdict.note: I tried to refute this finding and could not; it holds. Reference count, outside the definition (h:61-62) and the evaluateFlight signatures (h:179, cpp:66): 1 production construction (segment_chain_planner.cpp:3251), 1 installed example (flight_evaluator_example.cpp:18) and 1 Korean usage-doc snippet (planning_computation_usage_ko.md:162), plus 8 constructions in flight_evaluator_test.cpp (:104, 130, 151, 178, 246, 259, 297, 336). The 3 non-test references are all constructions. The finding's '6 code references / 4 files' is roughly right if the definition and declarations are counted. Every current caller passes named lvalues, so there is no existing bug. This is a latent API hazard for new external users. It matters because the struct is a showcased public, installed-consumer entry point: the example comment says it is usable 'without constructing a planner, PathManager, ROS node'. The misreading example is plausible because the doc snippet builds `phases` with exactly the brace form a user would naturally inline. No rename is needed; the name 'Input' is accurate. Minimal non-breaking fix: declare deleted overloads `FlightEvaluationInput(poly_traj::Trajectory&&, const std::vector<PhaseSpan>&) = delete;` and `FlightEvaluationInput(const poly_traj::Trajectory&, std::vector<PhaseSpan>&&) = delete;` (plus the both-rvalue combination). None of the 11 constructions above would break, since all pass lvalues. Also move the 'arguments must outlive this object until evaluateFlight returns' rule onto the constructor comment. The alternative is to have the struct own copies of the phases, which are cheap; that changes the semantics and is a design choice, not a rename. This is not a suspected bug: no runtime re-verification is needed because no current call site passes a temporary. Medium priority, not high, because the fix is a small header-only addition with zero caller churn, and the hazard currently has no live trigger.

finding.issue: These fields carry hidden sentinels. A ground floor applies only if ground_height > -0.5 (route_slice_solver.cpp:27, direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24); struct defaults are -1.0 (= disabled), while PathManager's member default is -0.1 (= enabled; path_manager.h:797). raw_max_z defaults to -1e9 (= no restoration). The units (absolute world z in u) and the sentinel rule are not stated in either header.
finding.misreading_example: A user flying over terrain below sea level sets ground_height = -0.8 u (absolute, -80 m) and silently loses the floor clamp, because anything <= -0.5 means 'no ground'. Or a user leaves the default -1.0, expecting PathManager's -0.1 behaviour.
finding.reason: The names are fine. The undocumented magic threshold is a contract gap shared by two public configs. Document 'absolute z in u; <= -0.5 disables the floor (legacy sentinel)', or later replace it with std::optional<double>, which is not a rename.
finding.affected_callers: RouteSliceConfig: 14 code references / 8 files (path_manager.h/.cpp, route_slice_*, segment_chain_planner.*). DirectAltitudeConfig: 4 code / 3 files, 5 test references.

verdict.evidence: Header text: route_slice_solver.h:27-29 says only "Snapshot of the PathManager-owned settings"; the field at :36 `double ground_height{-1.0};` has no comment giving units or a sentinel. The struct comment at :11-13 covers only RouteSliceRequest (u, u/s). direct_trajectory_solver.h:17-19 documents `raw_max_z` as "the route's maximum z before denoising" but does not explain the -1e9 "no restore" default (:20). `ground_height{-1.0}` at :23 has no comment. Implementation: route_slice_solver.cpp:27 and direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24 both use `if (config.ground_height > -0.5)` and otherwise skip the floor. direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:21 uses `std::max(path_max_z, config.raw_max_z)`, so -1e9 is a no-op. The sentinel rule is written down elsewhere: path_planner/include/path_planner/dyn_a_star.h:115 ("Sentinel: <= -0.5 disables the plane") and config/optimizer_params.yaml:572-573 ("<= -0.5 disables"). Contradicting comment, which the original finding missed: path_manager.h:790-796 says "If set >= 0 ... A value < 0 (e.g. the default -0.1) disables that plane". The code treats -0.1 as enabled (-0.1 > -0.5 at route_slice_solver.cpp:27, dyn_a_star.cpp:382/1575/1760, poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:655/837/1197). Units are stated only at path_manager.h:797 ("absolute world z; 1 u = 100 m"). Feeding paths: path_manager.cpp:475-479 (sliceSolveConfig passes ground_height_ positionally) and path_manager.cpp:1617-1619 (DirectAltitudeConfig aggregate init).
verdict.note: Confirmed, and partly understated. The names are fine and should not change. The real gap is the undocumented sentinel `> -0.5` (enabled) / `<= -0.5` (disabled), together with unstated units (absolute world z in u). The finding missed something more serious: an existing comment is wrong. path_manager.h:790-796 says "< 0 (e.g. the default -0.1) disables". In the code, -0.1 enables the floor in the slice and direct band paths and in A*. The yaml (optimizer_params.yaml:572-573) and dyn_a_star.h:115 state the correct rule. Fix: (1) In route_slice_solver.h:36 and direct_trajectory_solver.h:23, document "absolute world z in planner units (1 u = 100 m); <= -0.5 disables the floor (legacy sentinel shared with A*/optimizer)". (2) In direct_trajectory_solver.h:20, document that raw_max_z -1e9 means "no pre-denoise ceiling to restore". (3) Correct the misleading path_manager.h:790-796 comment. Treat it as a doc bug, not a code bug. The behaviour is consistent across modules; only that comment disagrees. The same undocumented sentinel also appears in RouteQueryConstraints::ground_height/virtual_ceiling (route_search_backend.h:41-42) and OptimizerEnvironment (optimizer_environment.h:38-39). Document them all at once. On the below-sea-level misreading example: it is plausible but niche. The more likely misreading comes from trusting the path_manager.h comment. A later switch to std::optional<double> would break the positional aggregate initialisation at path_manager.cpp:479/1617-1619 and in tests direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp:131,147,158,224-226. It would also have to stay consistent with the shared -0.5 sentinel in dyn_a_star/poly_traj_optimizer. So it is low value now; doc-only is enough. review.area_summary:
B2_geometry_risk_phases (path_manager): read-only naming and boundary audit of mission_geometry.h, terrain_risk.h, zone_policy.h, risk_zone.h, terminal_phase.h, transition_phase.h, waypoint_eval.h and terrain_data.h. I read them against their .cpp files, their main callers (path_manager.cpp, segment_chain_planner.cpp, flight_evaluator.h/.cpp, planning_environment_store.cpp), the CMake install/export setup and docs/design/modularized_function_api_ko.md.

Overall verdict: no mass rename is needed. Most names in this area say what they do, and many already carry units in the name (_m, _mps, _s, u). The real problems fall into four groups.

(1) One name that actively misleads about units: `EntryCandidate::route_start_s` and `TransitionResult::route_start_s`. The `_s` suffix means seconds on every other field in transition_phase.h, but this value is an arc length in planner units.

(2) The terrain callbacks. Four of them share one shape, `std::function<bool(double,double,double*)>`, under three names, and the units differ:
- `TerminalPhase::helixDescent(..., terrain_z)` takes planner units.
- `TransitionRequest::terrain_z` and `waypoint_eval::SafetyHooks::terrain_z` take metres.
- `FlightEvaluationEnvironment::terrain_elevation` has a different rule for what happens on a false return.
- `ElevationQuery` in mission_geometry is a fifth form: it returns a float sentinel instead of a bool.

(3) Contract issues where the name is fine but the stated contract is not:
- `ZonePolicySnapshot::valid` defaults to true (fail-open). flight_evaluator.h:65-67 has to force it to false. A test, flight_evaluator_test.cpp:70, relies on the true default.
- The two `TerrainData` accessors disagree about all-water cells: `getElevation` returns -inf, while `getElevationAndGrad` returns true with h=0. This is documented only inside the function bodies, not at the declarations.
- `synthesizeCommands` hides a 1.02/0.98 shrink of the speed window, and waypoint_eval.cpp has to back-solve it.
- The meaning of `valid` differs between a plan-wide snapshot and a per-leg snapshot.
- Units (planner u vs m) and invalid-elevation sentinels are not stated in mission_geometry.h or terrain_data.h. risk_zone.h hard-codes "1 unit = 100 m", while the chain reads a configurable `dynamics_unit_xy_m`.

(4) The public/internal boundary is blurry. Every header under include/ is installed (CMakeLists.txt:782). The documented public-header table (modularized_function_api_ko.md:59-70) lists only terrain_data.h and terrain_risk.h from this area. mission_geometry.h, zone_policy.h, terminal_phase.h, transition_phase.h and waypoint_eval.h are compiled into `path_manager_calculations` and installed, but their status is not stated. waypoint_eval has no production caller, only the two experiment tests. transition_phase.h exposes harness-only internals: `rk4Step`, `synthesizeCommands`, `wrapPi`, `invertPointMassCommands`, `pointMassAcceleration`.

Two behaviours look wrong and are reported separately as suspected bugs that need re-checking:
- `validateTransitionTrajectory` calls `req.zone_probe` without a null check, so a missing probe throws `std::bad_function_call`. It also silently skips the AGL gate when `terrain_z` is null, a case `generate()` refuses.
- `terminal_phase.cpp:79` calls `terrain_z` unconditionally.

Suggested priority:
- High: narrow rename of `route_start_s` (10 code references); fix the `ZonePolicySnapshot::valid` default, or at least document it.
- Medium: units for the `terrain_z` callbacks; the `TerrainData` water contract; a boundary table for the installed-but-unlisted headers; the `synthesizeCommands` contract.
- Low: everything else.

vocabulary_notes: Terrain lookup callback: one concept, five spellings/contracts. `ElevationQuery` = std::function<float(double,double)> with a -inf/<=-1e9 sentinel (mission_geometry.h:16). `terrain_z` in planner units (terminal_phase.h:50). `terrain_z` in metres (transition_phase.h:114, waypoint_eval.h:314). `terrain_elevation` where a false return must leave the output untouched (flight_evaluator.h:37). `PathManager::terrainElevation` returns false and leaves the output unwritten (path_manager.h:381). The terminal caller writes *e=0 on a false return (segment_chain_planner.cpp:3345), contradicting flight_evaluator.h:36.

Invalid-elevation sentinel thresholds differ for one concept: `elev > -1e9f` (mission_geometry.cpp:21), `elev > -1e10` (mission_geometry.cpp:91, 94), `e <= -1e9f` (path_manager.h:384), `std::isfinite(h)` (terrain_risk.cpp:78). All of them reject -inf, so behaviour is the same today, but the convention is not stated anywhere.

Planner-to-SI scale: `TransitionLimits::unit_xy_m/unit_z_m` (transition_phase.h:33-34), `waypoint_eval::FrameScale::unit_xy_m/unit_z_m` (waypoint_eval.h:79-81), ROS params `optimization/dynamics_unit_xy_m`/`dynamics_unit_z_m` (segment_chain_planner.cpp:1566-1568). Meanwhile the comments hard-code the scale as '1 unit = 100 m' (risk_zone.h:12, terrain_risk.h:12-13). The scale is configurable and anisotropic in one place and a fixed constant in another.

Policy trust: 'measured' (`routeSearchPolicyMeasured`, route_search_backend.h:133; `last_search_policy_measured_`, path_manager.cpp:2215), 'valid' (`ZonePolicySnapshot::valid`, zone_policy.h:31), 'knowledge' (`RoutePolicyKnowledge::CANONICAL_DISPOSITIONS`, route_search_backend.h:86-91), 'legacy_pass' 1..3 = FM2 3-pass (route_search_backend.h:98-100). The prose also says 'canonical policy' and 'Contract 2' (zone_policy.h:22, 29). These are related but distinct, and no header maps them onto each other.

Disposition enum has two names: `RouteZoneDisposition` (canonical, route_search_backend.h:79) and the alias `ZoneDisposition` (zone_policy.h:13, re-aliased again at path_manager.h:475). Both are used about equally in code (28 vs 26 references).

Contact/verdict enums: `ZoneContactResult{CLEAR,CONTACT,STALE,INVALID}` (zone_policy.h:51), `transition_phase::ZoneProbe{CLEAR,CONTACT_STANDOFF,CONTACT_AUTHORED,STALE_OR_INVALID}` (transition_phase.h:88-93), `TrajectoryVerdict{OK,FAIL,STALE}` (transition_phase.h:195, where STALE also covers INVALID), `ReproductionMetrics::Verdict{kFail,kIncomplete,kPass}` (waypoint_eval.h:368), `ExtractStatus{kOk,...}` (waypoint_eval.h:146), `TransitionResult::ok + reason` (transition_phase.h:163-164). Enumerator spelling also mixes ALL_CAPS and kCamel between two headers of the same module.

'hard' vs 'authored' for one zone volume: `zone_hard_contacts` counts `ZoneProbe::CONTACT_AUTHORED` (waypoint_eval.cpp:926), and `FlightPhaseMetrics::zone_hard_n` is 'inside the AUTHORED volume' (flight_evaluator.h:99). Meanwhile `PathManager::zoneContact` CONTACT means the 1.05x routing volume, which the searcher calls `zoneHardVolumeContains` (path_manager.cpp:2310). So 'hard' means the authored volume in the metrics and the 1.05x volume in the searcher.

'env' is overloaded: environment (`PlanningEnvironment`, `environmentRevision`, path_manager.h:509) vs flight envelope (`env_peak_util`, `env_violation_steps`, waypoint_eval.h:340-341; `env_n`, `env_viol`, flight_evaluator.h:87).

Effective risk altitude: `terrain_risk::groundedZ` (terrain_risk.h:56) / `PlanningEnvironmentStore::groundedZ` (planning_environment_store.h:122) vs `PathManager::riskGroundedZ` (path_manager.h:721). The PathManager spelling is the clearer one.

Arc vs time: `traj_sampling::ArcTable{t, s}` uses s = arc (traj_sampling.h:25-27), and `SourcePath::s_m` = arc in metres (waypoint_eval.h:91). The `_s` suffix means seconds everywhere else in transition_phase.h (dt_s, t_max_s, dwell_s, duration_s), which collides with `route_start_s` = arc in planner units (transition_phase.h:73, 172).

Mission bounds vs map bounds vs BBOX: `computeMissionBounds`/`MissionBoundsResult` (mission_geometry.h:44, 61) feed `map_lower_bound_`/`map_upper_bound_` and are logged as '[BBOX]' / 'Map bounds' (path_manager.cpp:939-956), which then size the SDF (`ensureDistanceField`, path_manager.cpp:969).

finding.affected_callers: rg 'route_start_s': 10 code refs = transition_phase.h 2, transition_phase.cpp 3 (533, 593, 960), segment_chain_planner.cpp 3 (1754, 1902 comment, 1907). Tests: transition_experiment_test.cpp 3 (100, 683, 1028). Docs: transition_phase_contract.md 8, adr/0003-initial-vertical-6dof.md 1. No ROS param or message field, no examples.

verdict.evidence: The facts check out. In this header `_s` means seconds everywhere else: `dt_s` :35, `t_max_s` :36, `dwell_s` :56, `knot_dt_s` :63, `blend_t_max_s` :64, `duration_s` :173. `EntryCandidate::route_start_s{0.0}` :73 has the comment "arc on the committed route (planner units)". `TransitionResult::route_start_s{-1.0}` :172 has no comment and sits right above `double duration_s{0.0};` :173, next to `poly_traj::Trajectory traj; // PLANNER UNITS` :168. Production code treats the field as arc length everywhere: segment_chain_planner.cpp:1754 `e.route_start_s = arc[static_cast<size_t>(idx)];` with `arc = routeArcTable(route)` from :1749; segment_chain_planner.cpp:1907 `cutAtArc(route, cap, tr.route_start_s, ...)`; transition_phase.cpp:533 sorts candidates by it ("ascending arc order" :528); transition_phase.cpp:593 prints it as `entry_s=%.1f`; transition_phase.cpp:960 `out.route_start_s = entry.route_start_s;`. Neighbouring code already uses a `_u` suffix (`rl.turn_radius_u` :1739, `rl.accel_arc_u` :1740, "chain/phase/arrive_min_arc_u" :1744). There is one mitigation. The `s` follows the usual Frenet arc-parameter convention, and docs/transition_phase_contract.md:121 says it outright ("호장 `route_start_s`", i.e. arc length `route_start_s`). The prefix is deliberate, not a slip. But the header's own field-suffix convention conflicts with it. The header is installed through CMakeLists.txt:782 `install(DIRECTORY include/)`, yet its only production consumer is segment_chain_planner.cpp:13, plus waypoint_eval.h:43, which includes it. No examples include it.
verdict.note: The finding is factually correct and the rename is cheap: 6 production refs (one is a comment) in 2 .cpp files, 3 test refs (transition_experiment_test.cpp:100, :683, :1028), 9 doc mentions (transition_phase_contract.md has 8, adr/0003 has 1), no ROS params, messages or examples. I agree with renaming both fields to `route_start_arc_u`. I lowered priority from high to medium for three reasons. (1) The struct belongs to the internal transition coordinator and is not part of the facade or request/result surface; its only production consumer is SegmentChainPlanner, and segment_chain_planner.cpp:1902 notes that the value is deliberately cut off before it goes further downstream. (2) The doc comment at :73 already settles the meaning for EntryCandidate, and the contract doc names it as arc length. (3) The `s` prefix is the standard arc-length symbol, so this is a clash between two conventions, not a mistake. The real gap is TransitionResult :172, which has no unit comment and sits next to `duration_s`. The reported misreading (passing it to `traj.getPos` or comparing it with `duration_s`) is plausible for anyone who reads only that struct. Minimum fix if the rename is deferred: add `// arc on the committed route (planner units), -1 = unset` at :172. If renamed, update the 8 places in transition_phase_contract.md, adr/0003-initial-vertical-6dof.md:301 and the TP-TRACE label at transition_phase.cpp:593 together. Not a bug: every use is consistently arc length. Docs references, including docs/design/api_naming_audit_2026_10_12/*, are not in caller_count.

Default-construction sites found: path_manager.cpp:2250 (overwritten at 2258), flight_evaluator.cpp:344 (overwritten by assignment), flight_evaluator.h:74 (overridden in the constructor), flight_evaluator_test.cpp:70 (relies on true).

verdict.evidence:
The facts check out. zone_policy.h:31 declares `bool valid{true};`. The comment at :23-30 says when it is false and that "an invalid snapshot is fail-closed at every consumer", but it never says what a default-constructed snapshot means. The authors knew the default is fail-open: flight_evaluator.h:63-68 has the FlightEvaluationInput constructor force `plan_policy.valid = false`, with the comment "External callers have not supplied measured policy". flight_evaluator_test.cpp:69-74 `policy()` never sets valid, so it relies on the true default. Every production writer sets valid explicitly: path_manager.cpp:2235 (`out->policy.valid = true` in captureLegPolicySnapshot) and :2258-2260 (zonePolicySnapshot, computed). flight_evaluator.cpp:344 `merged` is overwritten by a copy at :355. path_manager.cpp:1481 `LegPolicySnapshot lp` is filled by the capture and only pushed when the capture succeeds.

Three things lower the severity. (1) The canonical consumer PathManager::zoneContact (path_manager.cpp:2299-2311) returns INVALID on !valid, but it also returns STALE unless generation, epoch and ordered zone shapes all match the live state (zoneSnapshotCurrent, :2285-2296). A hand-built `ZonePolicySnapshot s;` with generation 0 and epoch 0 therefore comes back STALE, not CLEAR or CONTACT. zoneContactAuthored (:2318) and zoneExposureRaw (:2328) make the same check. Faking a match means copying the generation, epoch and shapes out of a real zonePolicySnapshot(), and that snapshot already carries a computed valid. (2) The default `Entry::disposition` is HARD_AVOID (zone_policy.h:35), the strictest policy, so default-filled entries do not invent exemptions. (3) The main external entry point already patches plan_policy (flight_evaluator.h:67), and segment_chain_planner.cpp:3262 assigns the real snapshot.

There is also one gap the finding missed, and it supports the contract issue. FlightEvaluationInput::leg_policies (flight_evaluator.h:75) is not patched. An external caller who builds `LegPolicySnapshot{i, i+1, {..., zones}}` gets policy.valid == true by default. flight_evaluator.cpp:157-160 then accepts it as measured per-piece policy, provided the zone count and contiguous serials line up, and report.missing_policy (:167) stays false. The verdict then depends on the caller's own zone_contact callback, and the test version of that callback (flight_evaluator_test.cpp:83-85) checks only s.valid.

Reference counts for `\bZonePolicySnapshot\b` (excluding reports, experiments and docs): 26 in total. 2 are in the defining zone_policy.h. 20 are in other production files: path_manager.h 6, path_manager.cpp 8, flight_evaluator.h 3, flight_evaluator.cpp 3, segment_chain_planner.cpp 2 (the earlier "22" double-counted the 2 zone_policy.h lines). 4 are in tests, all in flight_evaluator_test.cpp. No examples/ file references it. Field reads of `.valid` on snapshots in tests: chain_experiment_test.cpp (about 14), committed_route_test.cpp:177, route_search_backend_test.cpp:307/333, flight_evaluator_test.cpp:85/316/320/341. All of these read snapshots built by PathManager or set valid explicitly, except the helper at :70.
verdict.note: The name is fine; do not rename it. The contract issue is real: the default contradicts the documented fail-closed intent, and the authors already work around it in flight_evaluator.h:67. Priority drops from high to medium for two reasons. A default snapshot hits STALE at PathManager::zoneContact, because zoneSnapshotCurrent checks generation, epoch and shape. And the default disposition is HARD_AVOID, the strictest. As a result, the misreading example (a hand-built snapshot accepted as measured) only works if the caller copies a live generation, epoch and zone list. The strongest real exposure is FlightEvaluationInput::leg_policies: no constructor patches those entries, and flight_evaluator.cpp:157 checks only valid, the zone count and contiguous serials. Preferred fix (Option A): `bool valid{false};`. Every production writer already sets it explicitly (path_manager.cpp:2235 and :2258; flight_evaluator.cpp:355 copies). The only reliance on the default is the test helper at flight_evaluator_test.cpp:70, which would need `p.valid = true`. flight_evaluator.h:67 then becomes redundant but harmless. If behaviour must stay frozen, use Option B: add a line at zone_policy.h:31 saying the default is true and hand-built snapshots must set it, and add the same warning to FlightEvaluationInput::leg_policies. This finding is separate from any bug suspicion. No current production path was shown to misbehave. Before flipping the default, the owner should re-check (a build plus flight_evaluator_test and chain_experiment_test) that no aggregate initializer or `= {}` reset relies on true.

finding.issue: The two accessors look like 'the same surface, with or without the gradient' (the comment at :110 says 'Bilinear elevation + the ANALYTIC gradient of that same 0-blended surface'). Over an all-water patch, though, `getElevation` returns -inf ('water = no terrain', :93-99), while `getElevationAndGrad` returns true with h=0 ([WATER-FLOOR], :186-198). That difference is documented only inside the `...Uncached` body, not at either declaration. The declaration comment at :117-118 even says 'Returns false over pure water / outside the DEM', which contradicts :193-197, where pure water returns true with h=0.
finding.misreading_example: A user checks 'is there terrain here?' with `getElevationAndGrad(...)` and, trusting the comment at :117, treats a true return as land. Over open sea they get true and h=0, while `getElevation` at the same point says -inf / no terrain. The front-end (FM2) and optimizer views of the coast then disagree.
finding.reason: This is not a naming problem: both names are fine, and renaming would touch 29+13 references, including the rviz copy comments. The declaration comment at :117-118 is factually wrong for pure water, so fix the doc at both declarations and state the sea-level floor explicitly.
finding.affected_callers: getElevation: 29 references in 10 files (planning_environment_store, path_manager.h:383, terrain_risk.cpp:52/75, mission_geometry via ElevationQuery, rviz panels in comments). getElevationAndGrad: 13 references in 7 files (terrain_risk.cpp:151, path_optimizer via path_manager.cpp:617 comment, path_planner dyn_a_star.h:98 comment; tests 7).

verdict.evidence: The declaration comment at terrain_data.h:117-118 says "Returns false over pure water / outside the DEM (no terrain there)." The implementation contradicts it. getElevationAndGrad (:119) delegates to getElevationAndGradUncached (:147). For an all-NaN patch, the [WATER-FLOOR] branch at terrain_data.h:186-198 sets h=0, dhdx=dhdy=0 and returns true. It returns false only for !valid (:156) and off-DEM queries (:168-171). getElevation returns -inf for pure water (:93-99, `if (n00 && n10 && n01 && n11) return kInv;`) and for off-DEM (:76-78). Its one-line declaration comment at :41 does not mention -inf. The tests pin the divergence on purpose: terrain_risk_calculation_test.cpp:114 expects getElevation(...) == -inf ("pure water keeps no-terrain scalar sampler contract"), and :117 expects getElevationAndGrad(...) true with h==0 ("pure water keeps sea-level safety floor for gradient sampler"). So the behavior is intended and the declaration comment is stale. Readers are pointed at that stale comment too: path_manager.cpp:615-617 says "cost and gradient must agree exactly (see TerrainData::getElevationAndGrad)". The water difference is explained only inside the body, at :186-192 ("The front-end getElevation accessor retains its 'water = no terrain' behavior").
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/src/path_manager/src/terrain_risk.cpp:151 (groundedZ: `if (!terrain.getElevationAndGrad(...)) return pos.z(); // off-DEM: no terrain, no clamp`; relies on true-over-water)
verdict.note: The core claim holds: the comment at terrain_data.h:117-118 is wrong about pure water. The behavior is deliberate and the tests pin it, so this is a stale-doc problem, not a code bug, and fixing the comment is enough. Do not rename and do not change behavior. Suggested fix: rewrite :117-118 to say "Returns false only when !valid or the query is outside the DEM's physical rectangle. Over an all-water patch it returns true with h=0 and zero gradient (sea-level safety floor). Unlike getElevation, which returns -inf there, a true return does NOT mean land." Also expand the comment at :41 to say getElevation returns -inf when invalid, off-DEM, or over pure water, with coastal NaN corners blended as 0. Optionally mark getElevationAndGradUncached (:154) as a memo-bypass and test hook: its only references are terrain_data.h:147 and the test at terrain_memo_test.cpp:44. The finding's reference counts are inflated. Production code outside tests and the docs/validation snapshots has 4 getElevationAndGrad calls (terrain_risk.cpp:151; path_manager.cpp:620, :1303, :1892) and 12 getElevation calls (planning_environment_store.cpp x3, terrain_risk.cpp x2, path_manager.cpp x6, path_manager.h:383). Tests have 6 getElevation, 6 getElevationAndGrad and 1 Uncached reference, all under path_manager/test/. The rviz hits (trajectory_metrics_panel.cpp:585; altitude_profile_panel.cpp:1791, :1827) are comments only. The claimed path_planner dyn_a_star.h:98 reference was not found: there are no hits under mmp_path_planning/src/path_planner. Most of the larger counts come from frozen copies under mmp_path_planning/docs/validation/planning_visualization_2026_10_10/, which should not count as callers. The misreading example is plausible, because the declaration comment is exactly what a new user reads. No current production caller makes that mistake, though: groundedZ treats false as off-DEM, which matches the real behavior. So this matters for future users of the installed header (path_manager include dir, installed per CMakeLists.txt:697), not as a live defect. Medium priority because the cost is about two comment edits and the misleading text is on a public installed header.

finding.issue: The header says `lim` is 'the limit set whose speed window the thrust servo tracks' (:229). The implementation actually shrinks that window by 1.02/0.98: waypoint_eval.cpp:573-576 says 'synthesizeCommands brackets the servo with v_lo = end_speed_min * 1.02 and v_hi = end_speed_max * 0.98, so invert those factors', and back-solves `lim.end_speed_min_mps = v_cmd / 1.02`. A whole `TransitionLimits` is built just to pass a speed window. This hidden scaling is not in the declaration contract.
finding.misreading_example: A second follower calls `synthesizeCommands` with `lim.end_speed_min_mps = 120, end_speed_max_mps = 140` and expects the servo to hold any speed in [120, 140]. It actually tracks [122.4, 137.2], so the measured speed error is attributed to the vehicle instead of the hidden margin.
finding.reason: The name is fine. The undocumented 1.02/0.98 factors force callers to reverse-engineer them, as waypoint_eval.cpp:573-576 already does. State the factors in the header, or pass an explicit speed window. Callers are few and internal.
finding.affected_callers: synthesizeCommands: transition_phase.cpp (definition and generator use), waypoint_eval.cpp:580, 709. 8 references in 3 files, no test callers.

verdict.evidence: The header comment at transition_phase.h:227-229 only says "lim: the limit set whose speed window the thrust servo tracks". It does not mention any scaling. The implementation at transition_phase.cpp:203-205 computes `v_lo = std::max(lim.end_speed_min_mps * kSpeedTargetFrac, 1.1 * stall)` and `v_hi = lim.end_speed_max_mps * 0.98`. `kSpeedTargetFrac = 1.02` is file-local (transition_phase.cpp:68), and 0.98 is an unnamed literal. The servo then drives toward the nearest band point: `v_ref` at cpp:218-219 and thrust at cpp:223-225. The header says those law constants are deliberately kept file-local (transition_phase.h:214-219). waypoint_eval.cpp:573-577 reverse-engineers the factors with `lim.end_speed_min_mps = v_cmd / 1.02; lim.end_speed_max_mps = v_cmd / 0.98;`. waypoint_eval.cpp:705-707 repeats the same inversion without a comment. Only `lim.dyn`, `lim.end_speed_*` and `lim.capture_align_rad` are read, and `capture_align_rad` is discarded via `(void)capture_align_rad` at cpp:123,133. So a full `TransitionLimits` (h:31+) is built just to pass a speed window. The finding misses a second hidden term: v_lo is also floored at `1.1 * stall`, which depends on altitude (cpp:201-204). Neither the header nor the caller comment at waypoint_eval.cpp:573 mentions it. The header is installed through `install(DIRECTORY include/` at CMakeLists.txt:782, so it is reachable as public, but it is labelled as exposed for the WPE follower.
verdict.note:
I tried to refute this finding and could not; the claim is factually correct. Grep counts 8 textual hits across 3 files: 1 declaration, 1 definition, 2 comments and 4 call sites. There are no hits under test/ or examples. The name `synthesizeCommands` is fine, so it should not be renamed.

The real problem is a contract that is coupled across two files. The follower hard-codes 1.02 and 0.98 in two places to cancel a private constant (`kSpeedTargetFrac`) and a bare literal. If either factor changes in transition_phase.cpp, waypoint_eval silently servos to the wrong speed with no compile error. The finding also misses the `1.1*stall` floor on v_lo. Because of it, even the inverted band does not straddle `v_cmd` when `v_cmd` is near stall at altitude. I am not reporting this as a bug, because `v_cmd` is clamped to `dyn.speed_min_mps` first (waypoint_eval.cpp:568-569). Whether `speed_min_mps` ever falls below 1.1*stall at the evaluated altitudes needs runtime re-verification.

Two fixes, from smallest to fuller:
- (a) Document the 1.02/0.98 factors and the stall floor in the header, and replace the literals in waypoint_eval with a header-exposed constant or helper.
- (b) Add a narrow overload or helper that takes an explicit servo band (v_lo, v_hi), and keep the TransitionLimits form as a wrapper. This changes no behaviour, the cost is limited to the two internal callers, and it is a contract fix rather than a rename.

Medium priority holds because of the silent cross-file coupling. Option (a) alone would be enough to downgrade this to low.

review.area_summary: Area C_optimizer_api (path_optimizer package, namespace ego_planner). The new solve boundary is well named: OptimizerSolveRequest/OptimizerSolveResult/OptimizerSolveStatus, setRuntimeSettings/setEnvironment/setRiskEnvironment, seed/trajectory, edge_leg/piece_leg, TailBoundary prescribe_vel/prescribe_acc and buildPieceAltitudeCaps/buildPieceRoughness. Most of them should be kept. A rename is clearly worth it in only two places: (1) OptimizerSolveRequest::max_vel, which is really the seed and arrival cruise speed, while the same class has a separate optimization/max_vel limit; (2) the generic LOG_INFO/LOG_WARN/LOG_ERROR macros that leak from the installed poly_traj_optimizer.h into every path_manager consumer. Both are cheap now: 2 production callers for max_vel, and 0 external users of the macros. A free parameter-name fix (out_global/out_local to out_seed/out_trajectory) is also worth doing. The main problems are contract and documentation problems, not names. (a) Only waypoints.back() is used, as the tail position; all waypoints serve only as risk-barrier/taper anchors; path.front()/back() are replaced by head_pos and waypoints.back(). None of this is said in the request header. (b) Sentinel values are undocumented: ground_height/virtual_ceil_height <= -0.5 disables, and the default of -1 silently disables the crash-plane barrier for standalone users. Band z_hi < 0 means no cap. (c) The optimization/* yaml namespace is split. setParam ignores the lbfgs_*, collision_reject, audit_envelope_* and obstacle_clearance keys, which path_manager reads into OptimizerRuntimeSettings. (d) route_cost_profile claims to work in any consistent units, but it hard-codes constants on a 1 u = 100 m scale. (e) OPTIMIZER_FAILED also covers audit rejection, and the result comment says provenance survives refusal while piece_leg is always empty on failure. (f) optimizeFromPath is called the 'single replaceable seam', but it is non-virtual and superseded by solve(). (g) Legacy individual setters have no production callers outside the optimizer's own delegation, and they are not marked as compatibility API. The boundary also leaks internals: lbfgs.hpp, root_finder.hpp, FORMATION_TYPE, ConstrainPoints, the public OptimizeTrajectory_lbfgs, the public prepareRiskBarrier/markFrontEndCrossings, and a shared log_manager.hpp installed to <prefix>/common by three packages. I suggest documenting these, with no mass moves. No behaviour bug was confirmed. Two items are flagged for re-verification: a possibly uninitialized read of h in route_cost_profile.cpp:77 under a weak provider contract, and duplicate LogManager definitions compiled into two shared libraries. Reference counts exclude docs/, reports/ and experiments/. Code snapshots under docs/validation were seen but not counted.

findings.issue: The name says 'maximum velocity' (a limit), but the value is the desired cruise speed. It sets the seed time allocation (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:209, 218: des_vel = max_vel; time = seg_len/des_vel) and the arrival speed of an unprescribed tail (cpp:267: traj_end_vel = approach_dir * max_vel). The same class has a real limit read from optimization/max_vel (cpp:4119-4120, max_vel_). The header comment (optimizer_request.h:20-21) admits they are distinct, so the name contradicts its own documentation. The unit is u/s.
findings.misreading_example: A user sets request.max_vel = 3.0 (u/s) as a safety ceiling, expecting the optimizer to stay below it. In fact it sets every piece's seed duration and makes the default tail arrive at exactly 3.0 u/s, while the real speed limit comes from yaml optimization/max_vel.
findings.proposed_name: cruise_speed (u/s); optionally also rename the path_manager mirrors DirectTrajectoryRequest::max_vel and RouteSliceConfig::max_vel
findings.reason: This is a fresh API with only 2 production writers, so the rename is cheap now and expensive later. The confusion is high because the same class has a real max_vel limit. If the owner prefers no churn, at minimum rewrite the comment to say 'cruise speed used for seed timing and default tail arrival'.
findings.affected_callers: rg '\.max_vel\b' (code only): 22 refs, 17 in tests. Production: path_manager/src/direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:42, path_manager/src/route_slice_solver.cpp:40, path_optimizer/src/optimizer_session.cpp:70,85. path_manager.cpp sets request.max_vel = max_vel_ (manager/max_vel per route_slice_solver.h:31). Mirror fields: direct_trajectory_solver.h:54, route_slice_solver.h:33.

findings.issue: None of the boundary roles are documented. (1) Only waypoints.back() enters the trajectory, as the tail position (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:275). Every waypoint is used only as a risk-barrier exemption / moat-taper anchor (cpp:50 -> 3605-3607). Intermediate waypoints are NOT pass-through constraints. (2) The head state uses head_pos (cpp:274), not path.front(). The lead-in point is placed relative to path.front() (cpp:109), and the interior vertices path[1..n-2] become MINCO inner points (cpp:189-191). So path.front()/path.back() are ignored as positions. route_slice_solver.cpp:33 confirms this by passing waypoints = {goal_pos}.
findings.misreading_example: A user passes three mission waypoints and a coarse path, expecting the trajectory to fly through waypoint 2. Nothing enforces that. Or the user passes a path whose last vertex differs from waypoints.back(): the trajectory ends at waypoints.back(), and the last path vertex is silently dropped.
findings.reason: Keep the names; 'waypoints' matches the mission vocabulary used everywhere. Add a header contract: 'path: interior vertices seed MINCO pieces; endpoints are replaced by head_pos and waypoints.back(). waypoints: back() is the tail position; all entries (and head_pos) are risk-barrier exemption/taper anchors; intermediate entries are not constraints.' Optionally say what happens when path.front() != head_pos.
findings.affected_callers: waypoints: production writers direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:34, route_slice_solver.cpp:33. head_pos: 52 refs (27 test). The documentation change has no caller impact.

findings.issue: The fields carry undocumented sentinels and frames. They are absolute planner-frame z in u, and any value <= -0.5 disables the crash plane / virtual ceiling (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3300, 3313; the same check is copied in direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24 and route_slice_solver.cpp:27). The struct default of -1.0 therefore DISABLES the ground crash-plane barrier. The shipped yaml uses manager/ground_height: 0.02 (optimizer_params.yaml:563), and path_manager declares a different default, -0.1, which is enabled (path_manager.cpp:107). No height at or below -0.5 u (-50 m) can be expressed.
findings.misreading_example: A standalone user follows README.md:100-103: setParam(node), then setRuntimeSettings(OptimizerRuntimeSettings{}). The name 'ground_height = -1.0' reads like 'ground is 1 unit below zero'. In fact the safety crash plane is switched off, and terrain-free sea missions lose the ground barrier.
findings.reason: Renaming does not fix this; documentation does. State the frame (absolute planner z, u), the '<= -0.5 disables' rule, and that the default is disabled. Also consider aligning the struct default with the manager's behaviour, or make the disabled default explicit (for example a named constant kDisabledHeight). The default divergence between the struct (-1.0) and path_manager (-0.1) should be re-checked by the owner.

But the struct carries the L-BFGS numerical knobs (lbfgs_* :31-37), and the yaml keys optimization/lbfgs_*, optimization/collision_reject, optimization/audit_envelope_* and optimization/obstacle_clearance are read by path_manager (path_manager.cpp:526-597; obstacle_clearance at path_manager.cpp:199/464), not by setParam (setParam reads none of them; grep of poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3887-4204). findings.affected_callers: setRuntimeSettings: path_manager.cpp:601 (production), optimizer_session_test.cpp:174,347, optimizer_configuration_test.cpp:53. lbfgs_mem_size: 6 refs.

findings.issue: The header says the inputs are 'in the caller's consistent planner units; no normalization or new clamps occur', which implies the functions work in any unit. The implementation hard-codes constants on a 100 m/u scale: swath half-width kSwathR = 25.0 (route_cost_profile.cpp:52, i.e. 2.5 km), sampling step kStepMax = 2.3 (:59), AGL fade band kAglNear/kAglFar = 1.0/2.5 u (:250), and slope thresholds 0.2/0.8 (:225), which are dimensionless only when xy and z share one scale. The CMake comment (CMakeLists.txt:93-94) advertises these as reusable calculations.
findings.misreading_example: A reuser in a metres frame calls buildPieceAltitudeCaps. The swath floor then looks 25 m sideways instead of 2.5 km and samples every 2.3 m (slow), and the roughness AGL fade treats 1-2.5 m as terrain-following. The output is silently wrong.
findings.reason: The function names are fine. The documentation must say that the planner unit is 100 m (dynamics_unit_xy_m) and that xy and z are assumed to be the same scale, or the constants must become config fields (out of scope here). The owner should decide. This is not a naming issue.
findings.affected_callers: buildPieceAltitudeCaps: 28 refs (25 test), production only poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:157. buildPieceRoughness: 17 refs (14 test), production cpp:198.

findings.symbol: LOG_INFO / LOG_WARN / LOG_ERROR macros and global 'using LogManager'
findings.issue: The installed public header defines generically named macros whose bodies refer to members node_, drone_id_, log_manager_ and enable_debug_logs_. It also adds a global-namespace alias LogManager. path_manager/include/path_manager/path_manager.h:7 includes this header, so every path_manager consumer inherits the macros. The FSM uses prefixed FSM_LOG_* macros (replan_fsm.h:29-60), which shows the intended convention. All 66 uses are in poly_traj_optimizer.cpp.
findings.misreading_example: A consumer that includes path_manager.h and its own logging header (or defines LOG_INFO itself) gets a redefinition warning or error. Or the consumer writes LOG_INFO("x") in its own class and gets a confusing 'node_ was not declared' error that points into the optimizer header.
findings.proposed_name: Move the three macros into poly_traj_optimizer.cpp (or rename them POLY_TRAJ_OPT_LOG_INFO/WARN/ERROR); scope the alias inside ego_planner
findings.reason: No external caller uses them (0 references outside poly_traj_optimizer.cpp), so moving them costs nothing and closes a real header-hygiene leak.
findings.affected_callers: rg LOG_(INFO|WARN|ERROR)\( : poly_traj_optimizer.cpp 66, header 3 (the definitions), path_manager/path_planner 0. 'using LogManager' appears 2 times in code.

findings.issue: The comment says 'Diagnostic geometry/provenance survives backend refusal as well as success'. That holds for optimizer_path, but piece_leg (the provenance) is cleared on entry (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:45) and written only after L-BFGS success and audit pass (cpp:440-443). Tests assert that piece_leg is empty on refusal (optimizer_session_test.cpp:238, 290-292). path_manager.cpp:1650-1651 repeats the claim ('exact piece mapping on both result paths').
findings.misreading_example: A caller handling OPTIMIZER_FAILED reads result.piece_leg to blame the mission leg whose zone contact caused the rejection. It always finds an empty vector and concludes that tagging was lost upstream.
findings.reason: The behaviour is intentional and tested; only the wording is wrong. Change it to: 'optimizer_path survives refusal; piece_leg is filled only on SUCCESS and only when the edge_leg sizes matched'.
findings.affected_callers: piece_leg: 86 refs (32 test). optimizer_path: 35 refs (26 test). Documentation change only.

findings.issue: This value covers more than numerical failure. It also covers a converged trajectory discarded by the collision audit (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:1602-1607), the envelope reject gates (1622-1646), and the inner-point/time size mismatch (1345-1347). It is also the default-constructed status (:49). The path_manager wrappers additionally fold NOT_CONFIGURED/MALFORMED_INPUT into their own OPTIMIZER_FAILED (direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:57, route_slice_solver.cpp:43-44). planning_library_usage_ko.md:272-273 says deliberately not to subdivide.
findings.misreading_example: An operator sees OPTIMIZER_FAILED and retunes L-BFGS (g_epsilon, mem_size). The actual cause was setCollisionReject(true) discarding a fully converged trajectory that clipped terrain.
findings.reason: Keep the catch-all name; the design choice not to subdivide is documented elsewhere. The header should list what it includes ('L-BFGS failure or a post-solve collision/envelope audit rejection'). Splitting the value would be an API extension, not a rename, and the wrappers would lose the detail anyway.
findings.affected_callers: OPTIMIZER_FAILED: 12 refs (5 test). Mirrored by DirectTrajectoryStatus/RouteSliceStatus.

findings.issue: The comment calls it 'the single replaceable seam — a custom optimizer backend reimplements this' (h:661-663), but the method is non-virtual. PolyTrajOptimizer has no virtual functions (grep), so it cannot be reimplemented, and solve() (h:532) is now the boundary that wraps it (optimizer_session.cpp:83). The only production caller is solve() itself. path_manager.cpp:1606 still says 'Swap optimizeFromPath() to replace the backend'. Nothing in the header marks it as legacy or says that solve() adds admission checks and sets band/crossing state first.
findings.misreading_example: A new contributor subclasses PolyTrajOptimizer and overrides optimizeFromPath to plug in a different backend. solve() keeps calling the base version, because the call is statically bound.
findings.reason: Keep the name; equivalence tests rely on it (optimizer_session_test.cpp:93, direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp:89). Replace the 'replaceable seam' text with 'Compatibility entry; prefer solve(). Does not validate inputs, and uses band/crossing state left by setAltitudeBand/setSuppressCrossingExempt or by the previous solve().' Also fix path_manager.cpp:1606.
findings.affected_callers: optimizeFromPath: 9 code refs. Non-test: optimizer_session.cpp:83 (solve), the definition, the header, and the path_manager.cpp comments (1606, 1650). Tests: 2.

findings.issue: out_global receives the MINCO seed before L-BFGS (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:279), and out_local receives the optimized trajectory (cpp:432). 'global/local' reads as planning horizon (global plan vs local replanning window), which is the opposite of the actual roles. The new API already uses seed/trajectory (optimizer_request.h:52-53).
findings.misreading_example: A reader assumes out_local is a short receding-horizon window and out_global the full mission trajectory, and publishes out_global as the flown path. path_manager.cpp:1666-1671 documents exactly this past bug ('They were wired to the seed (out_global)').
findings.proposed_name: out_seed / out_trajectory
findings.reason: Parameter names are not part of the API or ABI, so the rename has zero caller cost and matches the new result fields.
findings.affected_callers: Callers pass the arguments by position: optimizer_session.cpp:83-86, optimizer_session_test.cpp:93-95, direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp:89-92. No source change is needed at call sites.

findings.issue: The name is a double negative and the field has no comment. True means: zones that the front-end route crosses do NOT get a barrier exemption, so the hard barrier stays armed (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3645-3649). It is set for pass-1 full avoidance (path_manager.cpp:1645-1646, builtin_route_search.cpp:142).
findings.misreading_example: A reader takes 'suppress crossing' to mean 'forbid the trajectory from crossing zones', and enables it hoping to avoid all zones. In fact it removes the crossing allowance only for zones the front-end route already crosses with visibility > 0.5. Zones containing mission points stay exempt (prepareRiskBarrier).
findings.reason: The term is used consistently in 15 non-test files (route_search_backend.h:109, route_slice_solver.h:24, segment_chain_planner.h:499-546, ...), so a rename would be a cross-module churn. Add one comment line at optimizer_request.h:36 (and route_search_backend.h:109).
findings.affected_callers: suppress_crossing_exempt: 41 code refs (15 test) across 15 non-test files. setSuppressCrossingExempt: 4 refs.

findings.issue: No comment on the type. z_lo/z_hi are absolute planner-frame z (u), not AGL (inferred from the request comment at :18 and path_manager computeDirectAltitudeBand). Sentinels: z_hi < 0 means no cap (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:649, 850), z_lo = -1e9 means no floor, weight 0 disables both (h:338-342). The default z_hi{-1.0} looks like a real altitude. path_manager has a parallel DirectAltitudeBand copied field by field (direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:41).
findings.misreading_example: A user in a frame where the sea surface is z = -2 u sets z_hi = -0.5 to cap altitude. The cap silently disappears because negative z_hi means 'off'. Or a user passes AGL values (z_hi = 3 u above terrain) and gets an absolute ceiling of 3 u.
findings.reason: The name is accurate. Document the frame and the sentinels. The type is only written via aggregate init at 2 production sites, so a later change of sentinels (for example std::optional) is also cheap.
findings.affected_callers: OptimizerAltitudeBand: 2 code refs (definition plus use in the request). band assigned at direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:41 and route_slice_solver.cpp:39.

findings.issue: The singular 'setParam' hides a full re-initialization with lasting side effects. It reads about 100 keys; it permanently declares every missing key on the node (declare_once, poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3902-3904); it keeps the node shared_ptr, which is later used for the clock and logging in each solve (cpp:1350); it resets parameters_initialized_ (cpp:3896, 4203); it rebuilds the vehicle model unless one was injected (cpp:4109-4111); and it replaces the swarm graph and formation (cpp:4194-4202). The comment for the overrides overload (h:507-508) says 'without temporarily mutating the shared ROS node', but the declarations are permanent node mutations.
findings.misreading_example: A user calls setParam(node) on a fresh node to 'set one parameter'. Afterwards the node lists about 100 optimization/* parameters with compiled defaults, which then shadow later yaml loading order. Or the user expects that the node is not retained and destroys it, but solve() still needs node_->get_clock().
findings.reason: 21 refs (14 test), and it is long-standing EGO-planner vocabulary. Renaming (for example configureFromRos) is optional and low value. Do fix the overload comment and list the side effects: declares missing keys, retains the node, resets formation/model.
findings.affected_callers: setParam(: 21 code refs (14 test). Production: path_manager.cpp:513. replan_fsm.cpp:43 references it in a comment.

findings.symbol: Legacy individual setters (setSDFManager, setTerrainHeightmap, setTerrainHeightGrad, setObstacleClearance, setCollisionReject, setEnvelopeReject, setLbfgsParams, setGroundHeight, setVirtualCeilHeight, setRiskGoalTaperRadius, setRiskZones, setRiskVisibility, setRiskShadowCeiling, setAltitudeBand, setSuppressCrossingExempt)
findings.issue: Only one general comment (h:520-522) says that 'old individual setters remain available for compatibility'. The setters themselves are not grouped or marked. Outside the optimizer's own delegation (optimizer_session.cpp:12-41, 80-81) they have no production callers, only equivalence tests. Some names also hide what they hold: setSDFManager stores a borrowed IDistanceField*, not a manager; setTerrainHeightmap takes a query function, not a heightmap. setAltitudeBand and setSuppressCrossingExempt are silently overwritten by every solve() (optimizer_session.cpp:80-81).
findings.misreading_example: A user calls optimizer.setAltitudeBand(...) once at setup and then calls solve(request) with a default band. The setup band is silently replaced by request.band (weight 0 = off).
findings.reason: Group these setters under a '// --- Compatibility setters: prefer setRuntimeSettings/setEnvironment/solve ---' banner. On setAltitudeBand/setSuppressCrossingExempt, note that solve() overwrites them. Do not rename: the names mirror path_planner/dyn_a_star.h setters (setTerrainHeightmap, setRiskVisibility, setGroundHeight), and the equivalence tests depend on them.
findings.affected_callers: Production use outside the optimizer is 0. Tests: setCollisionReject 5, setSDFManager 7, setAltitudeBand 2, setSuppressCrossingExempt 2, setLbfgsParams 1, setEnvelopeReject 1 (optimizer_session_test.cpp:72-80, direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp:85-87, 314-332). The same names on PathManager and PathSearcher are different methods and are unaffected.

findings.issue: The callback returns height AND gradient through out-params (x, y, float* h, float* gx, float* gy), and its bool result means 'over land / valid'. None of this is documented: argument order, units (gradient in u/u), whether outputs may be left unwritten on false. The field name 'terrain_gradient' suggests gradient only. route_cost_profile.cpp:77 declares 'float h, gx, gy;' uninitialized and reads h when the provider returns true, while buildPieceRoughness initializes them (:242).
findings.misreading_example: An integrator writes a gradient-only provider that fills *gx/*gy, returns true, and leaves *h untouched (the name says 'gradient'). buildPieceAltitudeCaps then reads an indeterminate h for the swath floor.
findings.reason: Document the signature (it fills height and gradient; returns false when no terrain). Optionally rename the field to terrain_height_gradient: only 5 refs, and it would match TerrainHeightGradientQuery. The uninitialized read is a possible UB under a weak provider. Re-verify it; with the current path_manager provider (getElevationAndGrad) it is likely benign.
findings.affected_callers: terrain_gradient: 5 refs (2 test), writer path_manager.cpp:616. TerrainHeightGradientQuery: 14 refs (8 test).

findings.issue: Both are public, and the docs tell callers to 'Call once per plan, after setRiskZones, before optimizing' (h:633-634). But optimizeFromPath already calls both at entry (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:50-51), which overwrites anything a caller prepared. No code outside the optimizer calls them.
findings.misreading_example: A user calls prepareRiskBarrier(start, custom_anchors) to exempt an extra zone before solve(). Their exemption is silently replaced by one computed from request.head_pos and request.waypoints.
findings.reason: Mark them as internal per-solve steps run by solve()/optimizeFromPath, and remove the 'call once per plan' instruction. Moving them to private is a cheap narrow follow-up (0 external callers), but it is not a rename.
findings.affected_callers: prepareRiskBarrier: 4 refs, markFrontEndCrossings: 4 refs. All are inside poly_traj_optimizer.h/.cpp; 0 tests.

findings.issue: 'Env' means flight envelope here, but the same class now has setEnvironment/OptimizerEnvironment. The returned value is a unitless utilization ratio (1.0 = at limit, comment h:587). After a rejected solve it still reports the discarded trajectory's peak, because checkCollision sets it before the reject gates (cpp:1709, 1815, then return false at 1607/1632/1646), while OptimizerSolveResult::envelope_peak stays 0.
findings.misreading_example: A user calls lastEnvPeak() after a failed solve() to 'see how close the environment got'. They read it as an environment or obstacle metric, and they also get a value for a trajectory that was never returned.
findings.proposed_name: lastEnvelopeUtilizationPeak (or deprecate in favor of OptimizerSolveResult::envelope_peak)
findings.reason: Only 1 production caller (optimizer_session.cpp:92) and 2 tests. The new result field already carries the value with clean failure semantics.
findings.affected_callers: lastEnvPeak: 4 refs total (2 test: optimizer_session_test.cpp, route_slice_solver_test.cpp).

findings.issue: The field has no comment. It is the peak flight-envelope utilization ratio (dimensionless, 1.0 = at the limit, poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:1815), and it is 0 unless the status is SUCCESS. 'peak' alone could be read as a speed or acceleration in u/s or m/s.
findings.misreading_example: A consumer compares envelope_peak against the vehicle's max speed in m/s.
findings.reason: The name is used consistently in path_manager (flight_evaluator.h, route_slice_solver.h:49, segment_chain_planner.cpp), 34 refs in total. A one-line unit comment is enough.
findings.affected_callers: envelope_peak: 34 refs (23 test) in 7 non-test files.

findings.issue: It only means 'setParam has not completed successfully' (optimizer_session.cpp:56 checks parameters_initialized_, which is reset at cpp:3896 and set at 4203). It does not detect a missing setRuntimeSettings or setEnvironment. A solve without them runs with member defaults (for example ground_height -1, which disables the crash plane) and no SDF or terrain.
findings.misreading_example: A user sees solve() return SUCCESS and assumes setup is complete. setEnvironment was never called, so the trajectory ignored terrain entirely.
findings.reason: Keep the name. State 'setParam not run or threw' in a comment, and list which bindings are optional and what their absence means.
findings.affected_callers: NOT_CONFIGURED: 5 refs (3 test).

findings.issue: It means fewer than 2 path vertices (optimizer_session.cpp:48), not a short geometric length. A zero-length 2-vertex path is accepted (midpoint insertion at poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:82-84; coincident-endpoint fallback at 260-265).
findings.misreading_example: A user expects a 5 m hop to return ROUTE_TOO_SHORT and handles it with a 'skip optimization' branch that is never taken.
findings.reason: The name is shared with DirectTrajectoryStatus and RouteSliceStatus (14 refs across 6 non-test files) and means the same thing there. Add '(fewer than two vertices)' as a comment.
findings.affected_callers: ROUTE_TOO_SHORT: 14 refs (7 test).

findings.issue: It checks vel and acc whatever the prescribe flags are. solve() admission checks only the prescribed components (optimizer_session.cpp:68-69). path_manager uses allFinite after anyPrescribed (ros_planning_backend.cpp:361-363, segment_chain_planner.cpp:379-381), so a tail that prescribes only velocity, with a NaN in its unused acc slot, is rejected there but accepted by solve(). The tail position is not part of TailBoundary; it is request.waypoints.back().
findings.misreading_example: A developer assumes allFinite() is the optimizer's admission rule and builds a validator on it. The two gates now disagree on vel-only tails.
findings.reason: TailBoundary's names (prescribe_vel/prescribe_acc, anyPrescribed, pinned) are clear and widely used (95 refs). Keep them. Document that allFinite is stricter than admission, or make it honour the flags (behaviour change; owner's call).
findings.affected_callers: allFinite on a tail: ros_planning_backend.cpp:363, segment_chain_planner.cpp:381. TailBoundary: 95 refs (15 test).

findings.issue: It stores 'const std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter> &overrides_' (:43). Constructing a named view from a temporary, for example 'RosParameterView v(node, {});', leaves a dangling reference. Current callers bind it to a function parameter, which is safe (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3897, path_manager.cpp:499). The snake_case has_parameter/get_parameter deliberately mirror rclcpp::Node so the templates duck-type. Keep them.
findings.misreading_example: A user writes 'const RosParameterView params(node, {{rclcpp::Parameter("optimization/max_vel", 2.0)}});' and later reads params, which is undefined behaviour.
findings.reason: 'View' already signals non-owning, and the comment says 'borrowed only while configuring'. Add 'do not construct from a temporary'. Optionally delete the rvalue constructor overload, which is a tiny change with no caller impact.
findings.affected_callers: RosParameterView: 5 refs. Production: poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3897, path_manager.cpp:499.

findings.issue: Return ranges and sentinels are undocumented. For shadow_ceiling, -inf means 'unshadowed' and stops relaxation for the whole piece (route_cost_profile.cpp:170); the value is absolute z. For visibility, the return is clamped to [0,1] (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3755), 0.5 is the exemption threshold (3603, 3643), and the gradient pointer may be null. visibility also has no named alias, unlike ShadowCeilingQuery.
findings.misreading_example: A provider returns 0.0 for 'no shadow' instead of -inf. Every piece in reach is then treated as shadowed at ground level, with cap candidates of -margin, and the shadow lift is silently skipped.
findings.reason: The names are fine. Add a contract line to each. Optionally add 'using RiskVisibilityQuery = ...' for symmetry; this is additive with no caller cost.
findings.affected_callers: ShadowCeilingQuery: 9 refs (5 test). shadow_ceiling: 25 refs. visibility: 11 refs.

findings.issue: Two structs share the name RiskZone in different namespaces, with different fields and different 'peak' semantics. ego_planner says 'raw yaml max_risk_level' and has vertical_reach. path_manager::RiskZone (risk_zone.h:11-14) says 'dimensionless in (0,1]; values >1 are field-capped' and has no vertical_reach. path_manager.cpp:614-621 converts one into the other, deriving vertical_reach. RouteCostZone (route_cost_profile.h:17-20) is a third projection (center+reach).
findings.misreading_example: Inside path_manager.cpp, where both types are visible, a reader sees RiskZone and assumes vertical_reach exists, or assumes optimizer peak values are pre-capped to 1.
findings.reason: Renaming ego_planner::RiskZone (for example to OptimizerRiskZone) touches few files: optimizer_environment.h, poly_traj_optimizer.h/.cpp, path_manager.cpp:620 and tests. The value is moderate, so it is optional. At minimum, align or explain the 'peak' comment and cross-reference the conversion. Keep RouteCostZone: a deliberately minimal Eigen-only projection.
findings.affected_callers: ego_planner::RiskZone in production: path_manager.cpp:620 plus optimizer internals. RouteCostZone: 6 refs (2 test). path_manager::RiskZone is spread through about 20 files and should not be touched.

findings.issue: The public header includes '../../common/log_manager.hpp' (poly_traj_optimizer.h:11). To satisfy this, three packages each install the same file to <prefix>/common, outside include/ (path_optimizer CMakeLists.txt:89, path_manager CMakeLists.txt:788, path_planner CMakeLists.txt:155). log_manager.cpp is compiled into both path_optimizer_lib (:53) and path_planner_lib (path_planner CMakeLists.txt:71), so swarm_formation::LogManager is defined in two shared libraries.
findings.misreading_example: A packager looking for public headers under include/ misses the common/ directory, so an installed consumer's include of poly_traj_optimizer.h fails. Or a consumer assumes LogManager belongs to path_optimizer and is surprised by duplicate definitions.
findings.reason: This is not a naming issue. Note the shared ownership in CMake and the docs. The duplicate symbol definitions are ODR-safe only while the sources are identical; flag for re-verification. A small shared target is a follow-up option, not part of this audit.
findings.affected_callers: 5 headers include ../../common/log_manager.hpp (poly_traj_optimizer.h:11, dyn_a_star.h:12, path_manager.h:9, replan_fsm.h:26, planning_environment_store.h:7).

findings.symbol: Installed internal headers and internal public members (lbfgs.hpp, root_finder.hpp, FORMATION_TYPE, ConstrainPoints, OptimizeTrajectory_lbfgs, getSwarmClearance, setControlPoints)
findings.issue: install(DIRECTORY include/) publishes every header, and poly_traj_optimizer.h pulls in lbfgs.hpp/plan_container.hpp/poly_traj_utils.hpp. Swarm and MINCO internals are public: FORMATION_TYPE, ConstrainPoints, OptimizeTrajectory_lbfgs (0 callers outside the optimizer), setControlPoints, and getSwarmClearance (non-const). Only poly_traj_utils.hpp (Trajectory in the result) and plan_container.hpp (SwarmTrajData used by path_manager.h:8, planning_execution.h:7, replan_fsm.h:25) have legitimate external consumers.
findings.misreading_example: A user treats OptimizeTrajectory_lbfgs as an alternative low-level API and calls it without the seed and cap tables, which only optimizeFromPath builds. The resulting state is inconsistent.
findings.reason: Do not move or decompose anything (MINCO/L-BFGS is out of scope). Add a header note: 'Supported API: solve(), setParam, setRuntimeSettings, setEnvironment, setRiskEnvironment, setVehicleModel, vehicleModel, dynamics* accessors; other public members are internal or compatibility.'
findings.affected_callers: OptimizeTrajectory_lbfgs: 4 refs, all in the optimizer. FORMATION_TYPE: 4. ConstrainPoints: 5. getSwarmClearance: 3 (path_manager.h:338-339 wrapper).

findings.issue: I checked these for promise-vs-behaviour mismatch. solve() takes the request by value and moves the path (optimizer_session.cpp:47). It returns an owned result. It sets the per-plan band and crossing policy every call (:80-81), so nothing is inherited from a previous solve(). It never exposes a partial seed on failure (:87). Status names match the path_manager wrappers.
findings.misreading_example: None significant. The one side effect worth knowing is that solve() leaves band and crossing state on the instance, so later legacy optimizeFromPath or inspectRiskCostAt calls inherit them.
findings.reason: Names accurately describe a synchronous, owned-result solve. Only the field-level documentation gaps above need work.
findings.affected_callers: solve(: 27 refs (24 test). Production: direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:44, route_slice_solver.cpp:42.

findings.issue: These looked suspicious but are correct. seed is the pre-L-BFGS MINCO guess (cpp:279) and trajectory is the optimized result (cpp:432). edge_leg (input, one tag per route edge) and piece_leg (output, one tag per MINCO piece) name the edge-to-piece mapping precisely (h:688-695). hasTrajectory() is the shared success predicate on four result types.
findings.misreading_example: 'seed' could be misread as an RNG seed by someone new to MINCO. The comment at :50-51 and the companion field 'trajectory' make the meaning clear.
findings.reason: These are accurate and consistent with path_manager. The edge/piece/leg vocabulary is one of the clearest in the codebase. hasTrajectory has 164 refs.
findings.affected_callers: edge_leg 130, piece_leg 86, hasTrajectory 164 (139 test).

findings.issue: Checked for ownership honesty. The OptimizerEnvironment comment (:50-57) says correctly that it is a live binding: zones and callbacks are owned, while the SDF pointer and captured providers are borrowed. 'Empty fields explicitly remove previous bindings' matches the implementation (optimizer_session.cpp:26-42). distance_field is a raw const pointer, which signals borrowing. terrain_cell_u uses the project-wide '_u' unit suffix.
findings.misreading_example: None from the names. The only risk is lifetime, and the comment covers it.
findings.reason: Good names and good ownership documentation. Keep.
findings.affected_callers: setEnvironment: path_manager.cpp:645 plus tests. setRiskEnvironment: path_manager.cpp:2363 plus tests. terrain_cell_u: 27 refs.

findings.issue: Checked whether 'build' hides side effects. Both are pure free functions: no globals, callbacks used only during the call, and results own their Eigen vectors (route_cost_profile.cpp:9-275). SCALAR_FALLBACK, ACTIVE and REFERENCE_MISMATCH match the code paths (:19-23, :205).
findings.misreading_example: None from the names. (The unit-scale issue is covered in a separate finding.)
findings.reason: Accurate verbs and status names. The only problem is the unit-scale documentation covered separately.
findings.affected_callers: buildPieceAltitudeCaps 28, buildPieceRoughness 17, PieceAltitudeCapStatus 11.

findings.issue: The imported name path_optimizer::path_optimizer_lib repeats the package name and adds '_lib'. The C++ namespace is the legacy ego_planner rather than path_optimizer. The target is not ROS-free: it depends on rclcpp (CMakeLists.txt:69-75; poly_traj_optimizer.h:8). The library_consumer README:43-44 says this honestly.
findings.misreading_example: A new user searches for path_optimizer:: types or assumes the target is ROS-free because of 'reusable library' wording in design figures.
