finding.issue: The name says 'maximum velocity' (a limit), but the value is the desired cruise speed. It sets the seed time allocation (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:209, 218: des_vel = max_vel; time = seg_len/des_vel) and the arrival speed of an unprescribed tail (cpp:267: traj_end_vel = approach_dir * max_vel). The same class has a real limit read from optimization/max_vel (cpp:4119-4120, max_vel_). The header comment (optimizer_request.h:20-21) admits they are distinct, so the name contradicts its own documentation. The unit is u/s.
finding.misreading_example: A user sets request.max_vel = 3.0 (u/s) as a safety ceiling, expecting the optimizer to stay below it. In fact it sets every piece's seed duration and makes the default tail arrive at exactly 3.0 u/s, while the real speed limit comes from yaml optimization/max_vel.
finding.proposed_name: cruise_speed (u/s); optionally also rename the path_manager mirrors DirectTrajectoryRequest::max_vel and RouteSliceConfig::max_vel
finding.reason: This is a fresh API with only 2 production writers, so the rename is cheap now and expensive later. The confusion is high because the same class has a real max_vel limit. If the owner prefers no churn, at minimum rewrite the comment to say 'cruise speed used for seed timing and default tail arrival'.
finding.affected_callers: rg '\.max_vel\b' (code only): 22 refs, 17 in tests. Production: path_manager/src/direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:42, path_manager/src/route_slice_solver.cpp:40, path_optimizer/src/optimizer_session.cpp:70,85. path_manager.cpp sets request.max_vel = max_vel_ (manager/max_vel per route_slice_solver.h:31). Mirror fields: direct_trajectory_solver.h:54, route_slice_solver.h:33.

verdict.evidence: The facts in the finding are correct. (1) The field is not a limit. It sets the seed timing: poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:209 has "const double des_vel = max_vel;" and cpp:218 has "seg_len / (des_vel * ...)". It also sets the arrival velocity when the tail is not prescribed: cpp:267 has "traj_end_vel = approach_dir * max_vel;", and the comment at cpp:239 calls this "full cruise speed at the goal". The real limit is a different value: optimization/max_vel is read into max_vel_ at cpp:4119-4120 and used as a soft penalty at cpp:3409 ("v.squaredNorm() - max_vel_ * max_vel_"). The optimizer_session.cpp:70 admission check only requires the value to be finite and positive, and :85 forwards it to optimizeFromPath(..., double max_vel, ...) (poly_traj_optimizer.h:683). (2) The codebase already uses the word "cruise" for this value. segment_chain_planner.cpp:1259 and :1719 have "const double cruise = pm_->maxVel();", and :2225-2226 says "mission-wide cruise speed". So the proposed name cruise_speed matches existing internal vocabulary, and it fits better than seed_speed because the value also sets a hard boundary condition on the tail. Mitigation: the confusion is already documented in four places. These are the struct comment at optimizer_request.h:20-21 ("max_vel is the seed/derived-arrival speed, distinct from its configured optimization/max_vel"), direct_trajectory_solver.h:51-53, route_slice_solver.h:31-32, and the usage guide docs/design/planning_library_usage_ko.md:270-271. The finding's fallback ("at minimum rewrite the comment") is therefore largely done already. What remains is moving the note onto the field itself and saying explicitly that it pins the unprescribed tail speed. Reference counts, using `.max_vel` with yaml/md and docs/validation excluded: 5 production field references outside the header (path_manager.cpp:1644, direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:42, route_slice_solver.cpp:40, optimizer_session.cpp:70 and :85), plus one positional aggregate init at path_manager.cpp:478 that a rename would not affect. Tests have 17 reference lines (optimizer_session_test.cpp 7, direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp 5, route_slice_solver_test.cpp 2, optimizer_configuration_test.cpp 1, route_slice_batch_test.cpp 1, vehicle_model_injection_test.cpp 1). Installed examples have 0 (path_manager/examples has no hits). A frozen historical consumer at docs/validation/planning_library_2026_10_08/historical/ext_c/optimizer_consumer/main.cpp has 7.
verdict.note: Weakened, not refuted. The name does contradict its own documentation, and a reader who sees only the name and signature could plausibly misread it. But the struct comment, both mirror comments and the usage guide already explain it, so a new user who reads the docs is not misled. Priority is therefore medium, not high. If the owner does the rename, do it as one coordinated narrow change across the three request structs (OptimizerSolveRequest, DirectTrajectoryRequest, RouteSliceConfig). The name cruise_speed is preferred over seed_speed_u_s because the value also pins the tail arrival speed (cpp:267). Leave the YAML key manager/max_vel and the optimizer parameter optimization/max_vel unchanged. Put a field-level comment on each struct that maps the field to manager/max_vel. Be aware that a narrow rename leaves several other spellings of the same value: PathManager::maxVel() (path_manager.h:221), the member max_vel_, the optimizeFromPath parameter max_vel (poly_traj_optimizer.h:683), and visualization RiskSettings::max_velocity (path_manager.cpp:1912). The owner should decide whether maxVel() becomes cruiseSpeed() in the same pass or stays with a comment. If there is no rename, the minimum doc-only fix is a per-field comment: "cruise speed (u/s): seed time allocation and level arrival speed of an unprescribed tail; not a limit". Separate issue, needs runtime re-verification and is not part of this rename: in segment_chain_planner.cpp:2228-2231, effMaxVel() falls back to pm_->maxVel() (manager/max_vel) when a worker has no optimization/max_vel override. It should probably fall back to the global optimization/max_vel. The same fallback is used at :2780 (ceil_v). The two values are both 2.0 in shipped config (optimizer_params.yaml:443, :449), so this does nothing today. If the two values diverge, the speed harmonization at :2237 and the ceiling-tail fix at :2784 could use the wrong ceiling. This is a direct consequence of the naming confusion the finding describes.

finding.issue: None of the boundary roles are documented. (1) Only waypoints.back() enters the trajectory, as the tail position (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:275). Every waypoint is used only as a risk-barrier exemption / moat-taper anchor (cpp:50 -> 3605-3607). Intermediate waypoints are NOT pass-through constraints. (2) The head state uses head_pos (cpp:274), not path.front(). The lead-in point is placed relative to path.front() (cpp:109), and the interior vertices path[1..n-2] become MINCO inner points (cpp:189-191). So path.front()/path.back() are ignored as positions. route_slice_solver.cpp:33 confirms this by passing waypoints = {goal_pos}.
finding.misreading_example: A user passes three mission waypoints and a coarse path, expecting the trajectory to fly through waypoint 2. Nothing enforces that. Or the user passes a path whose last vertex differs from waypoints.back(): the trajectory ends at waypoints.back(), and the last path vertex is silently dropped.
finding.reason: Keep the names; 'waypoints' matches the mission vocabulary used everywhere. Add a header contract: 'path: interior vertices seed MINCO pieces; endpoints are replaced by head_pos and waypoints.back(). waypoints: back() is the tail position; all entries (and head_pos) are risk-barrier exemption/taper anchors; intermediate entries are not constraints.' Optionally say what happens when path.front() != head_pos.
finding.affected_callers: waypoints: production writers direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:34, route_slice_solver.cpp:33. head_pos: 52 refs (27 test). The documentation change has no caller impact.

verdict.evidence:
The header doc (optimizer_request.h:18-24) covers only units, finiteness and max_vel. It never says what path, waypoints or head_pos do. optimizeFromPath's doc (poly_traj_optimizer.h:660-677) covers clean_path mutation, cap_ref_z and tail, but says nothing about waypoints.

The core claims hold:
- The head state is start_pos=head_pos (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:274; it is forwarded at optimizer_session.cpp:83).
- The tail position is waypoints.back() (cpp:275).
- Every waypoint plus start goes only to prepareRiskBarrier (cpp:50), where it becomes a taper anchor or exemption probe (cpp:3606-3607). waypoints.back() is also the goal for H4 commit and diagnostics (cpp:139, 186).
- Inner points come from clean_path[1..n-2] (cpp:188-191), and L-BFGS relaxes them freely ("inner point, so L-BFGS may relax it freely", cpp:103). So intermediate waypoints are not constraints.
- The lead-in point is anchored at clean_path.front() (cpp:109).
- route_slice_solver.cpp:33 passes waypoints={goal_pos}.

Overstated: "path.front()/path.back() are ignored as positions" is wrong. path.back() sets the default arrival heading, approach_dir = clean_path.back()-clean_path[n-2] (cpp:244-253). That heading feeds traj_end_vel (cpp:267). Both endpoints also set the seed time of the first and last pieces (seg_len, cpp:211-218) and the cap and roughness profiles (cpp:162-164, 197-198). They are not boundary positions, but they still change the result.

The docs make the misreading worse: planning_library_usage_ko.md:268-269 translates waypoints as "경유점" (pass-through point).

The tests keep the implicit invariant by hand: optimizer_session_test.cpp:59 sets r.path={r.head_pos, r.waypoints.back()}, and :331 sets later.waypoints.back()=later.path.back(). This confirms the invariant exists but is unwritten.
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/src/path_manager/src/direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:32-37 (copies DirectTrajectoryRequest.waypoints and head_pos; fed by path_manager.cpp:1634-1640 with all mission waypoints and start_pos)
verdict.note:
Do not rename. The fix is documentation only. This is not a suspected bug: the behaviour is consistent and the production callers already follow the implicit rules.

Counting: grepping the bare '.waypoints' and 'head_pos' identifiers mixes in unrelated structs (35/25 production hits, e.g. mmp_rviz_plugins/mission_command.cpp). The fields specific to OptimizerSolveRequest have only 2 production writers and 1 reader. The test count of 9 is OptimizerSolveRequest references: optimizer_session_test.cpp 6, optimizer_configuration_test.cpp 2, vehicle_model_injection_test.cpp 1. The historical consumers under docs/validation/.../ext_c also build this request.

Why priority drops to medium: path_manager is the only production writer and it supplies consistent inputs. The risk is limited to new users of the public solve(). Still, the Korean usage doc's "경유점" is an active source of the misreading.

Suggested header contract, corrected from the original finding:
- path: front() anchors the lead-in point. The interior vertices seed the MINCO inner points, which L-BFGS can relax, so they are not hard constraints. Endpoints are NOT boundary positions (head_pos and waypoints.back() are), but the final chord sets the default level arrival heading, and the endpoints affect the seed time and cap profile. Callers should keep path.front()≈head_pos and path.back()≈waypoints.back().
- waypoints: back() is the tail position and goal. All entries, plus head_pos, are risk-barrier exemption and moat-taper anchors. Intermediate entries are not pass-through constraints.

Mirror the same text in DirectTrajectoryRequest (direct_trajectory_solver.h:41-44), and replace "경유점" in planning_library_usage_ko.md:269.

Open question for runtime re-verification: what happens when path.back() differs from waypoints.back()? With a non-prescribed tail, the arrival heading then comes from a vertex the trajectory never reaches. The effect is unverified; I describe it only, not as a defect.

finding.issue: The fields carry undocumented sentinels and frames. They are absolute planner-frame z in u, and any value <= -0.5 disables the crash plane / virtual ceiling (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3300, 3313; the same check is copied in direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24 and route_slice_solver.cpp:27). The struct default of -1.0 therefore DISABLES the ground crash-plane barrier. The shipped yaml uses manager/ground_height: 0.02 (optimizer_params.yaml:563), and path_manager declares a different default, -0.1, which is enabled (path_manager.cpp:107). No height at or below -0.5 u (-50 m) can be expressed.
finding.misreading_example: A standalone user follows README.md:100-103: setParam(node), then setRuntimeSettings(OptimizerRuntimeSettings{}). The name 'ground_height = -1.0' reads like 'ground is 1 unit below zero'. In fact the safety crash plane is switched off, and terrain-free sea missions lose the ground barrier.
finding.reason: Renaming does not fix this; documentation does. State the frame (absolute planner z, u), the '<= -0.5 disables' rule, and that the default is disabled. Also consider aligning the struct default with the manager's behaviour, or make the disabled default explicit (for example a named constant kDisabledHeight). The default divergence between the struct (-1.0) and path_manager (-0.1) should be re-checked by the owner.
finding.affected_callers: ground_height: 18 code refs (4 test) in 9 non-test files. virtual_ceil_height: 18 refs (1 test) in 8 files. The struct is written only at path_manager.cpp:599-600 and in tests.

verdict.evidence: The public struct gives no frame, unit or sentinel. The comment block at optimizer_environment.h:22-24 covers only the struct's role. The fields read `double ground_height{-1.0}; double virtual_ceil_height{-1.0};` (optimizer_environment.h:38-39). The sentinel is documented only on PRIVATE members: poly_traj_optimizer.h:220-224 says "Sentinel: ≤ -0.5 disables the plane", and the public setters at poly_traj_optimizer.h:554-555 carry no comment. Behaviour matches the finding. poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3300 has `if (ground_height_ > -0.5 && p.z() < ground_height_)` with a barrier weight wei_ground_barrier_ (3308-3311). Line 3313 does the same for the ceiling. The same -0.5 rule appears at poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:655, 837, 1197; direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24; route_slice_solver.cpp:27; and dyn_a_star.cpp:382-383, 1575-1578, 1760-1761. setRuntimeSettings copies the fields straight through (optimizer_session.cpp:22-23). setParam does not read them; the only production writer is path_manager.cpp:599-600. The yaml documents it: optimizer_params.yaml:563-573 has `manager/ground_height: 0.02` with "<= -0.5 disables", and line 574 has `manager/virtual_ceil_height: -1.0   # <= -0.5 disables`. A STRONGER contract contradiction is in path_manager.h:790-798. It says "If set ≥ 0 ... voxelised as solid obstacle layers when the SDF is built ... A value < 0 (e.g. the default -0.1) disables that plane". path_manager.cpp:107-108 declares both parameters with default -0.1. Under the real -0.5 rule, -0.1 ENABLES both planes. No SDF voxelisation of ground_height_ shows up in the source tree (non-docs grep).
verdict.note:
I confirm the core claim: the public fields hide an absolute-z (u) frame and a "<= -0.5 disables" sentinel. With the struct default of -1.0, the ground crash-plane barrier is off. The misreading is plausible for a standalone user who follows README.md:101-104. That user calls setRuntimeSettings, and setParam(node) does not set these fields.

Corrections to the finding:
(1) The reference counts are inflated. The "18 refs" mix in different, same-named fields: RouteQueryConstraints::ground_height at route_search_backend.h:41, DirectAltitudeConfig at direct_trajectory_solver.h:23, RouteSliceConfig at route_slice_solver.h:36, the dyn_a_star/PolyTrajOptimizer private members, yaml keys and docs/validation copies. This exact struct field has 2 production uses per field (caller_count above counts per field), 2 test uses (optimizer_session_test.cpp:80-81), and no examples. optimizer_configuration_test.cpp:51 builds the struct but leaves these fields at their defaults.
(2) "Align the struct default with the manager" points the wrong way. The -1.0 default (disabled) is the same in every library layer: optimizer_environment.h, poly_traj_optimizer.h:223-224, dyn_a_star.h:116-117, route_search_backend.h:41-42 and route_slice/direct configs. path_manager's -0.1 is the outlier. Keep -1.0, and document it, or name it (for example kPlaneDisabled).
(3) A renaming is not needed. A doc comment on the two fields and the two public setters is enough. Add the same sentence to RouteQueryConstraints::ground_height/virtual_ceiling, which share the contract.

Separate SUSPECTED BUG (needs runtime re-verification, not a rename): path_manager.h:790-796 states the wrong rule ("< 0 disables") and a mechanism that looks stale (SDF voxelisation). path_manager.cpp:108 defaults manager/virtual_ceil_height to -0.1, which is > -0.5 and therefore ENABLED. If a launch omits the yaml key, a virtual ceiling at z = -0.1 u would penalise or block everything above -10 m in the optimizer (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3313) and in A* (dyn_a_star.cpp:383). The ground default of -0.1 likewise enables a plane at -10 m. The shipped yaml masks this (optimizer_params.yaml:563, 574). The owner should fix the path_manager.h comment and reconsider the -0.1 defaults. I would rate that part high.

finding.issue: The header says the inputs are 'in the caller's consistent planner units; no normalization or new clamps occur', which implies the functions work in any unit. The implementation hard-codes constants on a 100 m/u scale: swath half-width kSwathR = 25.0 (route_cost_profile.cpp:52, i.e. 2.5 km), sampling step kStepMax = 2.3 (:59), AGL fade band kAglNear/kAglFar = 1.0/2.5 u (:250), and slope thresholds 0.2/0.8 (:225), which are dimensionless only when xy and z share one scale. The CMake comment (CMakeLists.txt:93-94) advertises these as reusable calculations.
finding.misreading_example: A reuser in a metres frame calls buildPieceAltitudeCaps. The swath floor then looks 25 m sideways instead of 2.5 km and samples every 2.3 m (slow), and the roughness AGL fade treats 1-2.5 m as terrain-following. The output is silently wrong.
finding.reason: The function names are fine. The documentation must say that the planner unit is 100 m (dynamics_unit_xy_m) and that xy and z are assumed to be the same scale, or the constants must become config fields (out of scope here). The owner should decide. This is not a naming issue.
finding.affected_callers: buildPieceAltitudeCaps: 28 refs (25 test), production only poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:157. buildPieceRoughness: 17 refs (14 test), production cpp:198.

verdict.evidence: The header comment (route_cost_profile.h:50-51) says only "in the caller's consistent planner units; no normalization or new clamps occur". route_cost_profile.h:83 repeats "same synchronous borrowing/unit preconditions". Neither line names 1 u = 100 m, and neither says the hidden constants depend on scale. The implementation hard-codes those constants: route_cost_profile.cpp:52 `const double kSwathR = 25.0;` (the comment calls it "~ one piece length"), cpp:53-54 "2.3 u matched the 250 m full_map grid", which implies 100 m/u, cpp:59 `const double kStepMax = 2.3;`, cpp:225 `constexpr double kSlope0 = 0.2, kSlopeFull = 0.8;` (gradient magnitude, which is unitless only when xy and z share one scale), cpp:226-228 a literal 2.3 step, and cpp:250 `constexpr double kAglNear = 1.0, kAglFar = 2.5;` (cpp:246 says "1.0 -> 2.5 u band"). The config defaults also carry the scale: PieceAltitudeCapConfig headroom 0.4 and obstacle_clearance 0.5 at h:25,28. The deployed frame is xy = z = 100 m (path_manager/config/optimizer_params.yaml:463-464 dynamics_unit_xy_m/z_m: 100.0). The header is installed by CMakeLists.txt:84-86 install(DIRECTORY include/) and is pulled into the public optimizer_environment.h:4. The finding overstates one point. CMakeLists.txt:93-94 sits inside if(BUILD_TESTING) and says the test compiles the source "independent of the ROS optimizer adapter". It describes test isolation and does not advertise these calculations to outside consumers. The misreading example is also slightly off. In a metres frame the step is min(2.3, terrain_cell_u) (cpp:60-62), and the bigger effect is the swath shrinking from about 2.5 km to 25 m, not slowness. The core claim still holds: these are silent, scale-dependent constants behind a header that implies any consistent unit works.
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/src/path_optimizer/include/path_optimizer/optimizer_environment.h:4 #include route_cost_profile.h (type exposure only: TerrainHeightQuery/ShadowCeilingQuery used at :47,:60-61)
verdict.note: Keep both names. The finding agrees, and no rename is warranted. The fix is document-only. In route_cost_profile.h:49-51 and :82-84, state that the inputs are in the deployed planner frame (1 u = 100 m, xy and z the same scale, per dynamics_unit_xy_m/z_m). Also state that the internal swath (±25 u), sampling cap (2.3 u), slope band (0.2-0.8) and AGL fade (1.0-2.5 u) are tuned for that frame, so these functions are not unit-agnostic. Optionally, give the callback aliases at h:11-15 (x_u, y_u) -> h_u wording; supporting_review.md:26 already suggests this. I lowered the priority from medium to low because the only production callers are the optimizer's own adapter (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:157 and :198). No example, other package or installed consumer outside docs/validation historical copies calls either function directly, so nobody is misled in practice today. Turning the constants into config fields is behaviour-adjacent; it belongs to the owner and is not part of this audit. This is not a bug: the behaviour matches the deployed frame, and nothing needs runtime re-verification. Counts, excluding reports and experiments: buildPieceAltitudeCaps has 25 test references (src/path_optimizer/test/route_cost_profile_test.cpp) plus 1 production call. buildPieceRoughness has 14 test references plus 1 production call. Definitions and declarations are excluded. About 39 more references are in docs/validation historical consumer copies and design docs, and I counted them as neither production nor test.

finding.symbol: LOG_INFO / LOG_WARN / LOG_ERROR macros and global 'using LogManager'
finding.issue: The installed public header defines generically named macros whose bodies refer to members node_, drone_id_, log_manager_ and enable_debug_logs_. It also adds a global-namespace alias LogManager. path_manager/include/path_manager/path_manager.h:7 includes this header, so every path_manager consumer inherits the macros. The FSM uses prefixed FSM_LOG_* macros (replan_fsm.h:29-60), which shows the intended convention. All 66 uses are in poly_traj_optimizer.cpp.
finding.misreading_example: A consumer that includes path_manager.h and its own logging header (or defines LOG_INFO itself) gets a redefinition warning or error. Or the consumer writes LOG_INFO("x") in its own class and gets a confusing 'node_ was not declared' error that points into the optimizer header.
finding.proposed_name: Move the three macros into poly_traj_optimizer.cpp (or rename them POLY_TRAJ_OPT_LOG_INFO/WARN/ERROR); scope the alias inside ego_planner
finding.reason: No external caller uses them (0 references outside poly_traj_optimizer.cpp), so moving them costs nothing and closes a real header-hygiene leak.
finding.affected_callers: rg LOG_(INFO|WARN|ERROR)\( : poly_traj_optimizer.cpp 66, header 3 (the definitions), path_manager/path_planner 0. 'using LogManager' appears 2 times in code.

verdict.symbol: LOG_INFO / LOG_WARN / LOG_ERROR macros + global alias `using LogManager = swarm_formation::LogManager`
verdict.evidence:
The definitions are at poly_traj_optimizer.h:23 `#define LOG_INFO(msg, ...)`, :35 `LOG_WARN` and :42 `LOG_ERROR`. They sit in the global preprocessor namespace before `namespace ego_planner` (:48). Their bodies use the class members `enable_debug_logs_` (:183), `node_` (:192), `log_manager_` (:88) and `drone_id_`. The only comment, at :30-33, explains the WARN/ERROR routing change. It says nothing about scope or about being internal to the optimizer, so it does not resolve the problem.

The alias is at :14 `using LogManager = swarm_formation::LogManager;`. Its comment at :13 says "Forward declaration for LogManager", which is wrong: it is a global type alias, not a forward declaration.

The header is installed. path_optimizer/CMakeLists.txt:84 has `install(DIRECTORY include/ DESTINATION include)`, and :88-89 also installs common/log_manager.hpp "Required by the installed public optimizer header". path_manager/include/path_manager/path_manager.h:7 includes it. replan_fsm.h and segment_chain_planner.h include path_manager.h, so every path_manager TU and test inherits the macros.

The FSM uses prefixed macros: replan_fsm.h:29 `FSM_LOG_INFO`, :46 `FSM_LOG_WARN`, :53 `FSM_LOG_ERROR` and :60 `FSM_LOG_DEBUG`. common/log_manager.hpp:249-270 also uses distinct names (`LOG_INFO_CONDITIONAL`, etc.). The bare `LOG_*` names in the optimizer header are the outliers.
verdict.note:
I tried to refute this and could not. The finding holds, with one correction and one strengthening.

Counts (excluding reports/experiments and docs):
- A word-bounded search `\bLOG_(INFO|WARN|ERROR)\b` finds 66 uses, all in poly_traj_optimizer.cpp, plus the 3 definitions in the header.
- There are 0 uses in path_manager, path_planner, examples or tests.
- Other TUs include the header but never use the macros: optimizer_session.cpp, route_slice_solver.cpp, direct_trajectory_solver.cpp, path_manager.cpp, 2 optimizer tests and about 14 path_manager tests through path_manager.h.

Correction to the claimed callers: a non-bounded `LOG_(INFO|WARN|ERROR)\(` search also matches FSM_LOG_* (replan_fsm.cpp 39, replan_fsm.h 3). Those are different macros and do not count as callers. The finding's claimed counts stand once those are separated out.

Strengthening on the alias: the global `LogManager` alias at :14 has no unqualified users. Every use is spelled `swarm_formation::LogManager`: poly_traj_optimizer.h:88 and :533, plus forward declarations at builtin_route_search.h:7 and ros_planning_backend.h:9. So the right fix is to delete the alias, not to move it into ego_planner. The comment at :13 calling it a "Forward declaration" is also inaccurate.

Fix: move the three macros into poly_traj_optimizer.cpp after its includes, or keep them in the header with a POLY_TRAJ_OPT_LOG_* prefix and #undef them at the end. This changes no call sites and has no ABI or API effect on legitimate consumers. The only consumer that could break is one that accidentally relied on the leaked LOG_INFO or the global LogManager, and that is not supported use.

Plausibility: a new user who includes path_manager.h and defines their own LOG_INFO, or pulls in another library's LOG_INFO (glog-style and ROS1-era wrappers are common), gets a macro redefinition warning or error. A user who calls LOG_INFO in their own class gets errors about `enable_debug_logs_` or `node_`, which point into an optimizer header they never opened. That misreading is realistic.

This is header hygiene, not a behaviour bug. Medium priority is right because the header is installed and exported. It is not high, because no current consumer breaks. The `inf` global in dyn_a_star.h, mentioned in the sibling review, is a separate item and was not verified here.

finding.issue: The callback returns height AND gradient through out-params (x, y, float* h, float* gx, float* gy), and its bool result means 'over land / valid'. None of this is documented: argument order, units (gradient in u/u), whether outputs may be left unwritten on false. The field name 'terrain_gradient' suggests gradient only. route_cost_profile.cpp:77 declares 'float h, gx, gy;' uninitialized and reads h when the provider returns true, while buildPieceRoughness initializes them (:242).
finding.misreading_example: An integrator writes a gradient-only provider that fills *gx/*gy, returns true, and leaves *h untouched (the name says 'gradient'). buildPieceAltitudeCaps then reads an indeterminate h for the swath floor.
finding.reason: Document the signature (it fills height and gradient; returns false when no terrain). Optionally rename the field to terrain_height_gradient: only 5 refs, and it would match TerrainHeightGradientQuery. The uninitialized read is a possible UB under a weak provider. Re-verify it; with the current path_manager provider (getElevationAndGrad) it is likely benign.
finding.affected_callers: terrain_gradient: 5 refs (2 test), writer path_manager.cpp:616. TerrainHeightGradientQuery: 14 refs (8 test).

verdict.evidence:
The contract gap is real. route_cost_profile.h:12-13 defines `TerrainHeightGradientQuery = std::function<bool(double, double, float *, float *, float *)>` with no comment on what the arguments mean, what order they come in, their units, what the bool means, or whether outputs are written when it returns false. The nearby doc comments only cover precedence and lifetime: route_cost_profile.h:55-58 ("Callbacks are borrowed by reference only for this call... A present gradient provider takes precedence even when it returns false") and route_cost_profile.h:84-85 ("Failed gradient queries still count in the mean"). optimizer_environment.h:50-57 covers lifetime and rebinding only. The real contract is written down only on the provider, at path_manager/include/path_manager/terrain_data.h:110-120 (`getElevationAndGrad(world_x, world_y, float *h, float *dhdx, float *dhdy)`: "Bilinear elevation + the ANALYTIC gradient ... in WORLD (planning) coordinates ... Returns false over pure water / outside the DEM"). That header is in path_manager, not in the optimizer's public header.

The uninitialized read is factually correct. route_cost_profile.cpp:77-78 declares `float h, gx, gy;` and then evaluates `height_gradient(x, y, &h, &gx, &gy) && h > hmax`. buildPieceRoughness zero-initializes its outputs at route_cost_profile.cpp:242 (`float h = 0.f, gx = 0.f, gy = 0.f;`). The same reliance on "returns true implies *h is written" also appears inside the optimizer, at poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:787-789 and :1184-1186 (`float h, gx, gy; if (terrain_hgrad_(x, y, &h, &gx, &gy) && h > hmax)`). So the implicit contract is systemic, not local to one function.

The current provider is benign. terrain_data.h:146-150 always writes `*h = th; *dhdx = tgx; *dhdy = tgy;`, zero-initialized at :146, on both the true and false paths. The memo hit at :142-143 also writes all three. Under path_manager.cpp:618-621 no indeterminate read happens, so this is a hazard for third-party providers only, not a live bug.

The naming confusion is moderate rather than strong. The type name already says "HeightGradient", and the signature visibly has three float* outputs. Only the field name `terrain_gradient` (optimizer_environment.h:61) omits height. It also sits next to `terrain_height` (:60), which could suggest a gradient-only split. The same callback goes by other names elsewhere: `setTerrainHeightGrad`/`terrain_hgrad_` (poly_traj_optimizer.h:212,563) and `elevation_gradient` (path_manager/include/path_manager/route_search_backend.h:64).

Reference counts under src/, excluding reports and experiments:
- TerrainHeightGradientQuery: 5 production references (route_cost_profile.h:12,65,93 and route_cost_profile.cpp:15,218) and 8 test references (route_cost_profile_test.cpp:74,164,174,267,284,304,307,347).
- terrain_gradient: 3 production references (optimizer_environment.h:61, optimizer_session.cpp:31, path_manager.cpp:618) and 2 test references (optimizer_session_test.cpp:201,283).
- About 14 more hits are frozen historical snapshot copies under docs/validation/... These should not be edited and are not counted.
- No hits under examples.
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/src/path_optimizer/src/route_cost_profile.cpp:77-78 (uninitialized float h,gx,gy read after true return)
verdict.note:
I downgraded this to a documentation fix; a rename is optional. Recommended fix: add a comment at route_cost_profile.h:12. It should say that the callback takes (x, y) in world/planning coordinates and fills height *h in planner units plus dh/dx and dh/dy in *gx/*gy (unitless slope). It should say that a true return means terrain exists and that all three outputs must then be written. On false, outputs may be left unwritten and callers ignore them. Point optimizer_environment.h:61 to that comment, and note that terrain_data.h:110-120 is the reference implementation.

Renaming `terrain_gradient` to `terrain_height_gradient` is cheap: 2 production files and 1 test file, plus one public installed header. But it gives little benefit, because the type name already carries "Height". The three names for the same callback (`terrain_gradient` / `setTerrainHeightGrad` / `elevation_gradient`) are a separate, low-priority consistency item. Do not edit the docs/validation historical copies.

The uninitialized read is a latent risk, not a current bug. It happens at route_cost_profile.cpp:77 and at poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:788 and :1185. The current provider writes all outputs on every path (terrain_data.h:142-150), so it is benign today. It becomes undefined behavior only with a third-party provider that returns true without writing *h. If someone wants defensive hardening, zero-initializing at those declarations is a small change and does not touch the MINCO/L-BFGS internals. A runtime check is not needed to confirm the current provider is safe.

review.area_summary:
Area D (replaceable interfaces): VehicleModel (mmp_vehicle_dynamics), RouteSearchBackend with BuiltinRouteSearchBackend and the ROS config reader (path_manager), and the path_planner types reachable through them (PathSearcher, IDistanceField/SDFManager, risk_shape, FM2 GPU/eikonal headers, CMake exports). Overall verdict: KEEP the interface and class names (VehicleModel, FixedWingModel, RouteSearchBackend, BuiltinRouteSearchBackend, fixedWingTransitionParameters, routeSearchGeometryUsable). A mass rename is not justified. The real problems are mostly missing contracts and documentation, not bad names.
(1) Sentinels, units and frames that a custom implementer must know are not written in the interface headers: ground_height/virtual_ceiling (absolute frame z, <= -0.5 means disabled), IDistanceField units and sign, RouteSearchEnvironment providers, VehicleLimits/EnvelopeDomain floors, and penalty weighting/gradient units.
(2) Some precedence rules are implicit: RouteSearchProblem.model vs constraints.flight_path_angle_max_rad, and the policy identity echo.
(3) A few narrow renames have low caller counts and real misreading risk: nextRouteSearchIdentity, the global ::inf in dyn_a_star.h, astarSearchAndGetSimplePath (it also runs FM2), the two dynamicsParams() accessors with different contracts, the private fixedWingDynamicsGradCostPVA, and optionally the ros_route_search.h file name.
(4) Public/internal boundary leaks: fm2_gpu.h and eikonal_godunov.h are installed but internal. The BuiltinRouteSearchBackend::prepare adapter hook and the borrowed-searcher constructor argument are public. log_manager.hpp is installed into <prefix>/common. BuiltinRouteSearchBackend lives in the compatibility target path_manager_lib.
(5) One suspected bug, separate from naming and needing re-verification: the code default -0.1 for manager/virtual_ceil_height turns ON a ceiling at z = -0.1 under the searcher's '> -0.5' sentinel rule. A second, low-risk one: stale searcher flags are copied into an UNKNOWN policy.

The docs/validation/** source snapshot copies (planning_visualization_2026_10_10/source|harness, planning_library_2026_10_08/historical/ext_c) are reported separately. findings.issue: PathManager declares manager/virtual_ceil_height with default -0.1 (path_manager.cpp:108; member default path_manager.h:798). PathSearcher treats any value > -0.5 as an ENABLED ceiling (dyn_a_star.cpp:383, 1578, 1761). The shipped YAML uses -1.0 with the comment '<= -0.5 disables' (optimizer_params.yaml:574). RouteQueryConstraints defaults to -1.0 (route_search_backend.h:42). Without the YAML override, every cell with z > -0.1 frame units (about -10 m absolute) is blocked. ground_height uses the same -0.1 default (path_manager.cpp:107), which enables a floor at about -10 m.
findings.misreading_example: A library user constructs RosPlanningBackend with node overrides that omit manager/virtual_ceil_height. They expect 'no ceiling', the default most code reads as 'off'. In fact every route is blocked above z = -0.1 and the planner reports no route.
findings.reason: This is a behaviour issue, not a naming issue. The intended 'off' sentinel (-1.0, <= -0.5) is not the code default. Needs re-verification: check whether every production and test launch path always loads optimizer_params.yaml, and whether -0.1 was a legacy 'off' value from an older '> 0' rule.

finding.symbol: manager/virtual_ceil_height (and manager/ground_height) code default -0.1 vs the searcher's '> -0.5 enables' sentinel

PathSearcher treats any value > -0.5 as an ENABLED ceiling (dyn_a_star.cpp:383, 1578, 1761). The shipped YAML uses -1.0 with the comment '<= -0.5 disables' (optimizer_params.yaml:574). RouteQueryConstraints defaults to -1.0 (route_search_backend.h:42). Without the YAML override, every cell with z > -0.1 frame units (about -10 m absolute) is blocked. ground_height uses the same -0.1 default (path_manager.cpp:107), which enables a floor at about -10 m.
finding.misreading_example: A library user constructs RosPlanningBackend with node overrides that omit manager/virtual_ceil_height. They expect 'no ceiling', the default most code reads as 'off'. In fact every route is blocked above z = -0.1 and the planner reports no route.
finding.reason: This is a behaviour issue, not a naming issue. The intended 'off' sentinel (-1.0, <= -0.5) is not the code default. Needs re-verification: check whether every production and test launch path always loads optimizer_params.yaml, and whether -0.1 was a legacy 'off' value from an older '> 0' rule.
finding.affected_callers: Declaration path_manager.cpp:107-108, read path_manager.cpp:185-186, forwarded path_manager.cpp:1271-1272 into RouteQueryConstraints and path_manager.cpp:479, 599 into optimizer settings. verdict.symbol: manager/virtual_ceil_height and manager/ground_height (ROS parameter defaults); PathManager::virtual_ceil_height_ / ground_height_ member defaults
verdict.evidence: The defaults are -0.1: path_manager.cpp:107 `declare_parameter("manager/ground_height", -0.1)` and :108 `declare_parameter("manager/virtual_ceil_height", -0.1)`. The member defaults are also -0.1: path_manager.h:797 `ground_height_ = -0.1` and :798 `virtual_ceil_height_ = -0.1`. The comment beside them says the old rule: path_manager.h:789-796 reads "If set ≥ 0 ... A value < 0 (e.g. the default -0.1) disables that plane". It also says the planes are "voxelised as solid obstacle layers when the SDF is built", and I found no such SDF use, so that part is stale too. Every consumer uses the -0.5 sentinel instead. In the searcher, dyn_a_star.cpp:382-383, 1575/1578 and 1760-1761 test `> -0.5`, and the searcher's own doc at dyn_a_star.h:113-115 says "Sentinel: ≤ -0.5 disables the plane", with member default -1.0 at :116-117. The optimizer applies the same test at poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3300 and 3313 (`virtual_ceil_height_ > -0.5 && p.z() > virtual_ceil_height_`) and at 655, 837 and 1197. Slice solvers do too: route_slice_solver.cpp:27 and direct_trajectory_solver.cpp:24. So -0.1 turns both planes on: a ceiling at z=-0.1 u (-10 m) and a floor at -0.1. The values reach consumers through path_manager.cpp:1270-1271 (into RouteQueryConstraints, then builtin_route_search.cpp:66-67 into the searcher setters) and path_manager.cpp:599-600 (into optimizer runtime_settings, then optimizer_session.cpp:22-23). All other typed defaults are -1.0: route_search_backend.h:41-42, route_slice_solver.h:36, direct_trajectory_solver.h:23, optimizer_environment.h:38-39, poly_traj_optimizer.h:223-224. The shipped YAML optimizer_params.yaml:563 sets ground_height to 0.02, and :574 sets `virtual_ceil_height: -1.0   # <= -0.5 disables`. Every in-tree entry point loads that YAML: path_manager.launch.py:86, rviz_path_manager.launch.py:37-44, mission_planner_example.cpp:25, and every PathManager test via --params-file (for example committed_route_test.cpp:141, fsm_scenarios_test.cpp:133, ros_planning_backend_test.cpp:106, param_contract_test.cpp:82). So the defect is latent in the repo. It is still reachable through the public library path: RosPlanningBackend (ros_planning_backend.cpp:60-80) only merges caller NodeOptions overrides and never loads the YAML itself, and ros_planning_backend.cpp:89 says declare_parameter takes overrides "on first declaration", so a caller who passes no params-file gets the -0.1 code default.
verdict.note:
Confirmed from the source alone. The claim holds and is stronger than stated: the header comment at path_manager.h:789-796 says the -0.1 default "disables" the planes under an older "≥ 0 enables" rule. Every consumer now enables a plane for any value > -0.5. So the comment and the -0.1 defaults are leftovers from that older rule, and the comment itself misleads readers. This is not a naming problem, and no rename is warranted.

Reach is limited. The shipped YAML overrides both values (0.02 and -1.0), and every in-tree launch, example and test loads it. The only exposure is an out-of-tree caller of the public RosPlanningBackend or PathManager who passes no YAML. For that caller, the -0.1 ceiling blocks everything above -10 m, so search finds no route and the optimizer is pushed down toward -10 m.

Suggested narrow fix, not to be applied in this audit: change the defaults at path_manager.cpp:107-108 and path_manager.h:797-798 to -1.0, matching RouteQueryConstraints and the searcher. Rewrite the header comment to state the ≤ -0.5 sentinel and drop the stale SDF voxelisation sentence. A param_contract test could pin the default. One open question: should the code-default ground_height be -1.0 (off) or the shipped 0.02? That is a behaviour decision for the owner.

The test reference count of 5 covers the shared ground_height/virtual_ceil_height identifiers: direct_trajectory_solver_test.cpp:139 and 226, route_slice_solver_test.cpp:151, and optimizer_session_test.cpp:80-81. None of them pins the undeclared PathManager default. The caller count of 10 covers uses of the parameters or members in path_manager.cpp; across all production code the shared identifiers have about 30 references. I excluded the docs/validation snapshot copies. No runtime check was done because runtime is out of scope, but the static logic is unambiguous: -0.1 > -0.5.

finding.issue: The header gives defaults of -1.0 but does not say: (a) the values are ABSOLUTE frame-z planes (path_manager.h:797-798 says 'absolute world z'), not terrain-relative or AGL; (b) any value <= -0.5 means disabled (dyn_a_star.cpp:382-383); (c) units are frame units. 'ground_height' also collides with RouteSearchEnvironment::elevation (terrain).
finding.misreading_example: A custom backend author reads ground_height as terrain elevation or AGL clearance and applies it per (x, y). Or they treat -1.0 as a real plane 100 m below the origin and block everything under it.
finding.reason: The names are acceptable. The missing sentinel and frame contract is what every external RouteSearchBackend must reproduce to match the built-in one. Add a comment: 'absolute frame z, frame units; <= -0.5 disables'. A rename is not worth the cost because the field mirrors ROS parameter names.
finding.affected_callers: Producers: path_manager.cpp:1271-1272. Consumer: builtin_route_search.cpp:66-67. The struct name RouteQueryConstraints has 2 refs, both in the header. External implementers are unknown.

verdict.evidence: Definition: route_search_backend.h:37-47. The only comment there is "Shared physical query constraints, not algorithm tuning" (:37-38) plus the file-level note "Existing planner coordinates/units" (:16). Nothing at the field says the value is an absolute z, gives its unit, or names the sentinel. The contract exists only in internal headers. dyn_a_star.h:113-115 says: "Cells at or below ground_height_ (and at or above virtual_ceil_height_) are rejected ... Sentinel: ≤ -0.5 disables the plane." poly_traj_optimizer.h:221-222 gives the same "≤ -0.5 disables". The code matches them: dyn_a_star.cpp:382-383, 1575/1578 and 1760-1761 all use `ground_height_ > -0.5 && z < ground_height_` and `virtual_ceil_height_ > -0.5 && z > virtual_ceil_height_`. path_manager.h:797-798 says "frame units (absolute world z; 1 u = 100 m)". The producer is path_manager.cpp:1270-1271 (the finding cites 1271-1272, off by one). It copies ground_height_ and virtual_ceil_height_, which are loaded from ROS params "manager/ground_height" and "manager/virtual_ceil_height" (default -0.1) at path_manager.cpp:107-108 and 185-186. The consumer is builtin_route_search.cpp:66-67, which calls setGroundHeight and setVirtualCeilHeight. The name collision is real: route_search_backend.h:61 `std::function<float(double,double)> elevation` is the per-(x,y) terrain height, and it sits in the same RouteSearchProblem. Extra finding: path_manager.h:790-796 contradicts the sentinel. It says "If set ≥ 0, these altitudes are voxelised as solid obstacle layers when the SDF is built ... A value < 0 (e.g. the default -0.1) disables that plane." Under the real ≤ -0.5 rule, the default -0.1 is an ACTIVE plane at z=-0.1 in A*/FM2 (dyn_a_star.cpp:382). I also found no voxelisation of ground_height_ in path_manager.cpp. Its only uses are 185, 479, 599, 1270 and 1619. Minor point: dyn_a_star.h:114 says "at or below", but the code uses strict `<` and `>`.
verdict.note: Confirmed after an attempt to refute it. The header-local doc does not settle the confusion, and the misreading is plausible. A new backend author sees `ground_height` next to `environment.elevation` with no unit or sentinel, and could read it as AGL or terrain height, or treat -1.0 as a real plane. Counts (excluding reports/, experiments/ and docs/ snapshots): 2 production writes, path_manager.cpp:1270 and 1271. 2 production reads, builtin_route_search.cpp:66 and 67. 0 test references to these fields; route_search_backend_test.cpp:185 sets only flight_path_angle_max_rad. 0 example references. Same-named fields in other structs are separate symbols and were not counted: OptimizerEnvironment::ground_height (optimizer_environment.h:38), RouteSliceSolverConfig and DirectTrajectorySolverConfig ground_height (route_slice_solver.h:36, direct_trajectory_solver.h:23). Recommendation: keep the names. They mirror ROS params manager/ground_height and manager/virtual_ceil_height and internal setters, and the struct is public API, so renaming costs more than it gains. Add a field comment: "absolute frame z, frame units (1 u = 100 m); value ≤ -0.5 disables; reject z < ground_height / z > virtual_ceiling; NOT terrain/AGL — see environment.elevation". Note `virtual_ceiling` vs `virtual_ceil_height` is a small naming inconsistency, not worth churn. Separate suspected bug (doc/behaviour mismatch, needs runtime re-verification): path_manager.h:790-796 says a negative value such as the default -0.1 disables the plane and that ≥0 values are voxelised into the SDF. The actual sentinel is ≤ -0.5 (dyn_a_star.cpp:382-383, poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:3300), so -0.1 enables a plane at z=-0.1, and no SDF voxelisation is visible. This is likely harmless when terrain z ≥ 0, and the shipped yaml sets 0.02 (optimizer_params.yaml:563). Still, either the comment is stale or the behaviour is unintended. This is separate from the rename question.

finding.issue: The problem carries two sources for the same physical cone. constraints.flight_path_angle_max_rad comes from the explicit model override, else the live ROS parameter (path_manager.cpp:1276-1284). problem.model is the override, else the OPTIMIZER's model (path_manager.cpp:1273-1275), whose limits().flight_path_angle_max_rad can differ. The built-in backend ignores problem.model entirely (builtin_route_search.cpp:46-108). model can be nullptr when dynamics are off. None of this is stated in the header.
finding.misreading_example: An external backend uses problem.model->limits().flight_path_angle_max_rad, the natural source for a 'vehicle model'. It searches with a different climb cone from the built-in one whenever the ROS parameter and the optimizer model disagree. Or it dereferences a null model.
finding.reason: Document precedence on the field: constraints win, model is advisory or optional, and model may be null. No rename is needed.
finding.affected_callers: RouteSearchProblem: 12 non-test refs, 5 test refs. model is assigned only at path_manager.cpp:1273; no production reader of problem.model was found.

verdict.evidence: Header: route_search_backend.h:44-45 already says the constraints field is the "Resolved physical cone: explicit model limit, otherwise the ROS adapter reads the legacy live setting". That covers how the constraints field is filled. But `mmp_vehicle_dynamics::VehicleModel::Ptr model;` at :76 has no comment, so a reader is not told that it can be null, that it can disagree with the constraints, or which one wins. Producer: path_manager.cpp:1273-1275 sets `problem.model = vehicle_model_override_ ? vehicle_model_override_ : (context.optimizer && context.optimizer->dynamicsEnabled() ? context.optimizer->vehicleModel() : nullptr)`, so it is null when there is no override and dynamics are off. path_manager.cpp:1277-1284 takes the constraints value from the override, otherwise from the live `context.config.flight_path_max_deg`. The comment at :1278-1281 says the live read happens "even ... after a runtime parameter update". The optimizer model's cone comes from the same ROS parameter, but it is read only once, at init (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:4046-4050). After a runtime parameter change, `model->limits().flight_path_angle_max_rad` therefore differs from `constraints.flight_path_angle_max_rad`. Consumer: builtin_route_search.cpp reads only `problem.environment`, `problem.constraints` and `problem.identity` (lines ~50-51, 105), and uses the cone at :72 `setGeodesicSlopeTanMax(std::tan(constraints.flight_path_angle_max_rad))`. It never reads `problem.model`. Tests show the misreading is plausible. direct_plan_settings_test.cpp:76 reads `problem.model->limits().flight_path_angle_max_rad` with a null guard and asserts equality only on the explicit-settings path (:198-200), where both values come from the same temporary model. route_search_backend_test.cpp:235/327 only checks model identity. No test covers the ROS-live path where the two diverge.
verdict.note:
Counts cover src/ only, excluding reports/experiments and docs/. RouteSearchProblem appears 12 times in production code: route_search_backend.h 3, builtin_route_search.h 2, builtin_route_search.cpp 2, path_manager.cpp 3, path_manager.h 1, route_search_backend.cpp 1. It appears 5 times in tests: route_search_backend_test 3, direct_plan_settings_test 1, ros_planning_backend_test 1. Copies under docs/validation were not counted. Only path_manager.cpp:1273 writes problem.model, and no production code reads it. The only readers are tests (direct_plan_settings_test.cpp:75-76, route_search_backend_test.cpp:235). No example under src/path_manager/examples uses RouteSearchProblem.

All parts of the finding check out:
- The two sources can disagree when the ROS live parameter is changed at runtime, because the optimizer reads it only at init (poly_traj_optimizer.cpp:4046) while the search reads it live (path_manager.cpp:1277).
- The model is nullable.
- The built-in backend ignores the model.

The header comment at :44-45 only partly covers this. It explains where the constraints value comes from, but nothing on `model` says that the constraints value wins, that the model is advisory or optional, or that it may be null.

The divergence is designed behaviour, acknowledged in the comment at path_manager.cpp:1278-1281. It is not a bug, so a comment on the field is enough and no code change or rename is needed. Suggested wording at :76: "Optional (nullptr when dynamics are off and no explicit model). Informational only. The authoritative search cone is constraints.flight_path_angle_max_rad, and model limits may differ under the legacy ROS live-parameter path."

Medium priority is kept because RouteSearchBackend is the documented replaceable interface for external backends (see planning_library_usage_ko.md:221 on route_search_backend injection). An external author is likely to reach for problem.model. A field rename would break the 5 test references for little benefit.

finding.issue: Same name, different contract. PathManager::dynamicsParams returns const Parameters* from model->fixedWingTransitionParameters(), which is null for non-fixed-wing models (path_manager.h:591-597). PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams returns const Parameters& to the ROS fixed-wing snapshot regardless of the injected model (poly_traj_optimizer.h:589-593). The optimizer accessor has 0 callers in src.
finding.misreading_example: Code moved from the optimizer to the manager level calls optimizer.dynamicsParams() and gets the ROS fixed-wing numbers even though a custom model is injected. It silently uses the wrong airframe.
finding.proposed_name: PathManager::fixedWingTransitionParameters() (keep dynamicsParams as a deprecated forwarder); mark PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams as rosFixedWingSettingsSnapshot() or deprecate (0 callers)
finding.reason: The interface already established the precise name fixedWingTransitionParameters. The manager wrapper re-hides it under a generic name. Low caller counts make this cheap.
finding.affected_callers: PathManager::dynamicsParams: segment_chain_planner.cpp:1557, 1560, 1660 (3); tests chain_experiment_test.cpp:813, 1282, 3852, 3910 (4); docs snapshots 4. PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams: 0 callers.

verdict.evidence:
The facts in the finding hold. path_manager.h:591-597 returns a `const mmp_vehicle_dynamics::Parameters*` from `model->fixedWingTransitionParameters()`. It is null when vehicleModel() is null (optimizer not initialized or dynamics off, path_manager.h:584-589) and for model families other than fixed-wing. poly_traj_optimizer.h:589-593 returns `const Parameters&` to `dynamics_params_`, which is the ROS fixed-wing snapshot. The interface name `fixedWingTransitionParameters` is defined at mmp_vehicle_dynamics/include/mmp_vehicle_dynamics/vehicle_model.hpp:69 (virtual, default null) and overridden at :94.

The claim of confusion is weaker than stated, because both definitions already have comments that settle it. path_manager.h:591-593 says "Compatibility/capability accessor for the fixed-wing transition law. Other model families return null rather than supplying unrelated ROS fixed-wing settings". poly_traj_optimizer.h:589-590 says "Compatibility snapshot of ROS fixed-wing settings. With a custom model, use vehicleModel(); this snapshot is not its physical contract." The return types also differ: a pointer that can be null versus a reference. A call written as `const auto *dyn = optimizer.dynamicsParams();` does not compile, so code moved from the manager to the optimizer cannot switch silently. The reverse direction needs `auto&` or a copy, which also fails to compile. That makes the misreading example (silently using the wrong airframe) unlikely unless someone ignores both the comment and the type.

Reference counts (grep over src, excluding reports, experiments and docs snapshots):
- PathManager::dynamicsParams: 3 production references, all in segment_chain_planner.cpp (1557, 1560, 1660), and 4 test references in chain_experiment_test.cpp (813, 1282, 3852, 3910). Docs/validation snapshot headers contain 4 more copies, which are not callers. No examples use it.
- PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams: 0 references outside its definition.

The production callers already treat null as "this model cannot use the fixed-wing transition generator" (segment_chain_planner.cpp:1557-1559, error text "vehicle model does not support the fixed-wing 3DOF transition generator"). They match the documented contract, so there is no behaviour bug.
verdict.note:
The inconsistency is real, but the comments on both accessors and the different return types (nullable pointer vs reference) already keep it from causing silent misuse. The proposed misreading example would not compile as written.

Recommended action:
1. Leave PathManager::dynamicsParams as it is, or add a narrow alias `fixedWingTransitionParameters()` and keep dynamicsParams as a forwarder. Renaming the 3 production and 4 test call sites in a single file each is cheap but optional.
2. PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams has 0 callers. Mark it deprecated or move it to an internal section rather than renaming it. Before deprecating, check whether installed consumers outside src rely on it; I did not survey external or installed consumers.

Not a suspected bug. segment_chain_planner.cpp:1557-1563 handles the null case as the documented capability signal. Lines 1557 and 1560 overlap, since the null case is checked twice, but this is harmless.

Not reviewed: the docs/validation snapshot copies (4 header duplicates, not callers) and the implementation that fills `dynamics_params_` in poly_traj_optimizer.cpp.

finding.symbol: global constexpr double inf = 1e20 (and getFineGScoreSlice '+inf' doc)
finding.issue: An installed public header defines ::inf in the GLOBAL namespace with a FINITE value. It reaches every consumer of path_manager.h and planning_environment_store.h, which include dyn_a_star.h. getFineGScoreSlice says 'INFs left as +inf' (dyn_a_star.h:929), but unvisited cells hold 1e20. getCoarseG (coarse_g_ assigned inf at dyn_a_star.cpp:1567) is likewise 1e20.
finding.misreading_example: A facade user writes 'if (x == inf)' or 'std::isinf(slice[i])' expecting IEEE infinity and gets false. Or user code that defines its own global 'inf' fails with a redefinition error after including path_manager.h.
finding.reason: 5 uses, all inside path_planner (dyn_a_star.h:18, 40, 43, 44; dyn_a_star.cpp:1567). The global-namespace leak is real API pollution, so the cost is very low and the boundary gain is real. Also fix the slice doc to say '1e20'.
finding.affected_callers: Definitions/uses: dyn_a_star.h 4, dyn_a_star.cpp 1. Transitive exposure: path_manager.h, planning_environment_store.h, builtin_route_search.cpp, tests chain_experiment_test.cpp, risk_scenarios_test.cpp, terrain_pitch_test.cpp. Tests that define a local 'inf' (shadowing): optimizer_session_test.cpp:193, risk_contract_test.cpp:131, flight_evaluator_test.cpp:172.

verdict.evidence:
The finding's facts hold. The real problem is bigger than a name.

Leak:
- dyn_a_star.h:18 defines `constexpr double inf = 1e20;` before `namespace path_planner { namespace search {` (line 20), so it lands in the global namespace.
- The header is installed by path_planner/CMakeLists.txt:150 (`install(DIRECTORY include/`).
- Two public path_manager headers include it: path_manager/include/path_manager/path_manager.h:6 and path_manager/include/path_manager/planning_environment_store.h:5.
- Every facade consumer therefore gets a global `::inf` that is finite.

Docs that say "inf" but get 1e20:
- dyn_a_star.h:929 says "with INFs left as +inf", but `getFineGScoreSlice` returns `GridNode::gScore`, which defaults to `inf` (= 1e20) at h:40.
- dyn_a_star.h:189 says "inf if unreachable" for `coarse_g_`, which dyn_a_star.cpp:1567 fills with `coarse_g_.assign(N, inf)` (1e20).

Suspected bug (needs runtime re-verification). The code itself misreads its own sentinel:
- dyn_a_star.cpp:1650 counts `if (std::isfinite(coarse_g_[i])) ++n_reached;`. Since 1e20 is finite, the "reached" diagnostic counts every cell.
- dyn_a_star.cpp:1670-1671 reads `const double v = coarse_g_[...]; if (!std::isfinite(v)) return -1.0; // unreachable at coarse res`. This guard never fires.
- So `getHeuInadmis` (dyn_a_star.h:1047-1052) never takes its documented fallback, "Fallback (coarse field unavailable / cell unreachable): inflated euclidean". For unreachable coarse cells it returns `tie_breaker_*(1e20/step_size_)` instead.
- The `tie_breaker_*(1e20/step_size_)` result is a static reading of the code; it has not been run.

Contrast with code that uses real infinity:
- dyn_a_star.cpp:1846-1847 shadows the global with a local `const float inf = std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()` for fm2_T_, so FM2 holes are real +inf. That path is consistent; only the A*/coarse path uses 1e20.

Reference counts (rg -w inf over src, excluding reports/experiments):
- Real uses of global `::inf`: the definition at h:18, plus h:40, h:43, h:44 and cpp:1567. That is 1 use outside the header.
- Tests: 0 real references. optimizer_session_test.cpp:193, risk_contract_test.cpp:131 and flight_evaluator_test.cpp:172 each define a function-local `const double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()`. These shadow `::inf` and compile fine. The "redefinition" risk only applies to a consumer that declares `inf` at namespace scope.
- Examples: 0.
- Only test consumer of the 1e20 outputs: risk_scenarios_test.cpp:284 (`getCoarseG`) and :295 (`getFineGScoreSlice`), which dump raw binaries. Any offline reader that tests isinf on them gets it wrong.
verdict.note:
The rename itself is cheap and worth doing: 5 internal uses, no test or example callers. It also removes a global-namespace symbol from installed public headers.

Proposed name: move it into `path_planner::search` as `kGridScoreUnset` or `kUnreachedCost`. Do not call it `kGridInf`, because the problem is that it is not infinity.

The finding missed something more important. The 1e20 sentinel contradicts the code's own `std::isfinite` checks at dyn_a_star.cpp:1650 and :1671. That makes the documented "cell unreachable -> euclidean fallback" in getHeuInadmis (h:1050-1051) dead code, and makes the reached-cell diagnostic wrong.

Handle it as two separate items:
(a) Contract / suspected bug, needs runtime re-verification. Either test `>= kUnreachedCost` or use `std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()`, and update the comments at h:189 and h:929.
(b) Narrow rename and move into the namespace.

Changing the value to real infinity could affect the SMHA* dispatch arithmetic, which compares `f_inadmis <= w*f_anchor`. Compare A* outputs before and after.

Impact is lowered by the comment at h:1055-1059, which says the A* grid is the ablation/fallback path and FM2 is production. That is why this stays medium, not high.

review.area_summary: Area E (environment/execution stores, ROS backend + adapters, remaining PathManager/SegmentChainPlanner/ReplanFSM public surface, CMake target split). Overall verdict: KEEP almost all names. The split is sound. PlanningEnvironmentStore owns the live world. PlanningExecutionStore owns the slot, IDs and revocation. PathManager is the adapter that coordinates them. RosPlanningBackend is the explicit ROS compatibility backend. The compute (no adoption) vs plan (compute + apply) verb convention holds for PathManager, SegmentChainPlanner and RosPlanningBackend; the only exception is planCommittedRoute, which plans a route and never adopts. The real problems are contract and documentation gaps, not naming taste: (1) ExecutionReceipt.applied is true for accepted no-product failures and then reports the slot's PREVIOUS trajectory_id. (2) The compute* entry points are not side-effect free: they persist overrides, set formation on the optimizer, publish viz, and through prepareRoute->flushPendingObstacles can revoke the active flight and emit an ABORT. (3) Several header comments are stale: PathManager add* return codes, the SegmentChainPlanner::compute doc block, and the ReplanFSM callback-group/threading doc. (4) Users of the new compute API must reach the legacy PathManager through RosPlanningBackend::executionManager() to apply a result, so the new/legacy boundary leaks. (5) "Global" means three different things (the whole-mission direct solve, the reference/seed slot, and /planning/initial_trajectory). Narrow renames are justified only where caller counts are tiny and the name actively misleads: ExecutionRevocation::detected_time (trajectory-relative, wire name detected_trajectory_time), invalidateStoredTrajectoryForEnvChange (hard-codes POLICY_UNEVALUATED, 1 caller), PathManager::dynamicsParams (same name as the optimizer's, different contract), and optionally setTransitionActive, SegmentChainPlanner::segments() and deliverTrajToOptimizer. A rename of computeGlobalTrajectory or planGlobalTraj is not worth the cost now; document instead. Thread/serialization expectations are stated per method in most headers, but there is no class-level statement on PathManager, and the one explicit threading comment in replan_fsm.h is wrong. One suspected behaviour issue needs re-verification: the abort's detected trajectory time is the check start t0, not the time of the blocked point. Caller counts exclude reports/, experiments/, docs/ and the docs/validation snapshot copies; test references are counted separately.
