vocabulary_notes: Execution slot has five names: PlanningExecutionStore::current() (planning_execution.h:38), PathManager::executionTrajectory() (path_manager.h:148), type LocalTrajData (plan_container.hpp:30), 'active slot' (planning_execution.h:55), and 'stored trajectory' in revalidateStoredTrajectory/invalidateStoredTrajectoryForEnvChange (path_manager.h:435,455). They are consistent enough to keep. Add a one-line glossary in planning_execution.h.

'Global' is overloaded: computeGlobalTrajectory/planGlobalTraj mean the whole-mission direct solve (path_manager.h:117,152), and its product.trajectory goes to the LOCAL/execution slot. GlobalTrajData/referenceTrajectory() (path_manager.h:149), globalTraj2ROSMsg (replan_fsm.h:99) and global_path_pub_ on /planning/initial_trajectory (replan_fsm.cpp:219-220) mean the reference/seed slot. planFromGlobalTraj (replan_fsm.h:110, private) neither plans nor uses a global trajectory: it publishes the stored execution trajectory (replan_fsm.cpp:516-555).

Environment change counter vocabulary: the field name is environment_generation (planning_computation.h:38, mission_plan.h:57, planning_execution.h:21, seal/apply/revoke params, wire TrajectoryExecutionControl.environment_generation), but it is filled from PathManager::environmentRevision() (path_manager.h:507) = PlanningEnvironmentStore::revision() (planning_environment_store.h:111-113, a SUM). Component counters are zoneGeneration()/zonePolicyGeneration() (planning_environment_store.h:110, path_manager.h:496) and TerrainData::generation. Related: 'epoch' = front-end search run (zonePolicyEpoch, path_manager.h:513), 'serial' = search_serial (path_manager.h:491), 'fingerprint' = zone content hash (path_manager.h:449). Keep the names (the wire field is fixed) and document the mapping.

'Identity' is overloaded: trajectory IDs (identity_advances, previous_identity_counter in planning_computation.h:34,45; identityCounter() in planning_execution.h:42), the execution context (execution_context in planning_computation.h:43, built from nextRouteSearchIdentity() in planning_execution.cpp:10), and route-search request identity (problem.identity.context_id/request_id). One allocator named for route search issues IDs for an unrelated execution context.

Adoption verbs: apply (PlanningExecutionStore::apply in planning_execution.h:47; PathManager::applyPlanningComputation in path_manager.h:145), adopt (adoptEmergencyTrajectory :51, private adoptCurrent :63), 'commit' for a front-end route (commitRoute in segment_chain_planner.h:104, CommittedRoute, planCommittedRoute in path_manager.h:168). 'commit' never means execution adoption. Keep, but say so in the glossary.

Withdrawal verbs: revoke (store, planning_execution.h:59), invalidate (invalidatePending :44, invalidateStoredTrajectoryForEnvChange path_manager.h:455, SegmentChainPlanner private invalidateStoredTrajectory, which only sets a flag on the computation), withdraw (comments), ABORT (wire/ReplanFSM::publishExecutionAbort). ExecutionRevocationReason has an alias EnvChangeReason (path_manager.h:434), and the wire uses REASON_*.

Owner/store/manager/backend: classes are named *Store, but their comments call them 'owner' (planning_environment_store.h:59, planning_execution.h:27, replan_fsm.h:126-128 'private environment and execution owners'). PathManager is called 'manager', 'adapter', 'live manager' and, via RosPlanningBackend::executionManager(), 'execution manager'. MissionPlanningBackend/RosPlanningBackend/RouteSearchBackend use 'backend' for both planning implementations and search strategies.

Obstacle vocabulary: the public value types are SphereObstacle/BoxObstacle/DynamicObstacle (planning_environment.h:32-42). The store uses EnvironmentObstacle/PendingEnvironmentObstacle (planning_environment_store.h:34-49) with addSphere/addBox, and the adapter/facade use addDynamicSphere/addDynamicBox/clearDynamicObstacles. Return codes >=0/-1/-2 are documented three times, and one copy is wrong (see findings).

Terrain transition vocabulary: TerrainGridUpdate{NO_CHANGE,CLEAR,REPLACE,REJECTED} (ros_terrain_grid.h:11) vs TerrainUpdateKind{REJECTED,CLEARED,REPLACED} (planning_environment_store.h:51). A null message is NO_CHANGE in one and REJECTED in the other. Terrain setters: setTerrain(TerrainGrid) (backend/facade), setTerrainData(GridMap) (PathManager, RosPlanningBackend, TerrainData), ingestTerrain (store).

Unit suffixes are mixed inside one class: cruiseFloorUnits() and effectiveHandoffMaxMps() carry units, but maxVel() (path_manager.h:221, manager/max_vel in planner units/s) does not. In the start-state API, _u (pos_u/vel_u, junction_pva_tol_u) is consistent and good.

findings.issue: applied==true means 'the computation was accepted and its context consumed', NOT 'a trajectory was adopted'. An accepted no-product failure, or a refusal that only invalidates, returns {true, current_.traj_id, drone_id}, where current_.traj_id is the PREVIOUS (possibly just-invalidated) flight's ID. The header has no comment on this. Only docs/design/planning_computation_usage_ko.md:79-80 shows that hasTrajectory() must be checked after applied.
findings.misreading_example: A new caller writes `auto r = mgr->applyPlanningComputation(c); if (r.applied) publish(c.product->trajectory, r.trajectory_id);`. For an accepted failure, product may be absent (crash), or the post-gate rejected intermediate product may be present (product kept for legacy ID effects), and it gets published under the old flight's ID.
findings.proposed_name: keep `applied`; add a doc comment, and optionally an additive `bool adopted_trajectory` (true only when a product was adopted)
findings.reason: The name is defensible (the effect was applied), but the struct is the public outcome of the new compute->apply contract and its two failure semantics are invisible at the declaration. An additive field is cheap. Renaming `applied` would touch about 40 sites for no gain.
findings.affected_callers: Receipt `.applied` reads: non-test 7 (ros_planning_backend.cpp:221; path_manager.cpp:1104,1118,1774; segment_chain_planner.cpp:259,2526 and 3133 via apply). Tests: planning_execution_test.cpp 18, execution_adoption_test.cpp 10, chain_experiment_test.cpp 3, committed_route_test.cpp 1. The design doc example is planning_computation_usage_ko.md:77-80.

findings.issue: 'compute' consistently means 'no execution adoption', but the methods are not side-effect free. RosPlanningBackend::compute persists length_per_piece/obstacle_clearance on the manager (ros_planning_backend.cpp:278-281), may initOptimizer (301-304), calls setFormationInfo (314), and pushes formation into the optimizer after a successful solve even if the result is never applied (327). All three paths go through prepareRoute, which calls ensureDistanceField and flushPendingObstacles (path_manager.cpp:970,978). flushPendingObstacles -> revalidateAfterEnvChange -> revoke can withdraw the ACTIVE flight and fire the observer, which publishes an ABORT on the wire (replan_fsm.cpp:234-237). Compute also advances the policy epoch and rewrites the compatibility route accessors (path_manager.cpp:1033,1047) and publishes RViz previews. Only planCommittedRoute's comment (path_manager.h:164-167) lists the revoke/abort effect. computeGlobalTrajectory's comment (114-116) and the backend's (36-38) mention it only vaguely.
findings.misreading_example: A user calls backend->compute(candidate_request) speculatively during a flight to compare alternatives and discards the result. They expect no effect on the vehicle, but a queued obstacle gets installed, the current flight is revoked and an ABORT is published, and the next mission inherits the candidate's obstacle_clearance override.
findings.reason: Keep the verb. compute vs plan is the one convention that is applied consistently across all three classes, and renaming would cost more than it helps. List the exact persistent and live effects once, in ros_planning_backend.h, and reference that list from the other two headers.
findings.affected_callers: RosPlanningBackend::compute: ros_planning_backend.cpp:215 + execution_adoption_test.cpp 7 calls. computeGlobalTrajectory: 16 non-test refs (path_manager.cpp 6, segment_chain_planner.cpp 6, ros_planning_backend.cpp 1, header 3), 10 test (direct_plan_settings_test 9, chain_experiment_test 1). SegmentChainPlanner::compute: ros_planning_backend.cpp:318, segment_chain_planner.cpp:258.

findings.issue: It returns the full mutable std::shared_ptr<PathManager>, not an execution-only handle. Through it the FSM sets terrain, risk zones and obstacles and revalidates (replan_fsm.cpp:1227,1295-1312,1436,1457). The official compute->apply recipe also has to go through it (planning_computation_usage_ko.md:77-78), because RosPlanningBackend exposes compute() but no apply(). Calls made through the returned pointer skip the backend's requireInitialized() and its value-API validation (setTerrain/encodeTerrainGrid).
findings.misreading_example: A reader assumes executionManager() gives a narrow execution-control facade, so environment updates must still go through the backend. They then call executionManager()->setRiskZonesRuntime(...) and executionManager()->setTerrainData(...) freely, unaware that this bypasses the backend contract. Or they assume no public apply step exists for compute() results.
findings.proposed_name: add RosPlanningBackend::apply(const PlanningComputation&) -> ExecutionReceipt; optionally narrow-rename executionManager() -> legacyPathManager() and keep the old name as an inline alias
findings.reason: The name promises less than it gives, and the missing apply() forces new-API users onto the legacy class. Adding apply() fixes the contract additively. A rename is optional, and cheap if an alias is kept.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test 1 (replan_fsm.cpp:176). Tests 14 (ros_planning_backend_test.cpp 9, execution_adoption_test.cpp 3, chain_profile_contract_test.cpp 1, vehicle_model_injection_test.cpp 1). Docs example planning_computation_usage_ko.md:78.

findings.issue: 'Global' here means the whole-mission direct solve. The returned PlannedTrajectory::trajectory is adopted into the LOCAL/execution slot (executionTrajectory()), and only reference_trajectory goes to GlobalTrajData/referenceTrajectory(). In ReplanFSM, 'global' means the reference/seed published on /planning/initial_trajectory (globalTraj2ROSMsg, global_path_pub_).
findings.misreading_example: A reader assumes computeGlobalTrajectory computes what referenceTrajectory()/GlobalTrajData holds (the seed or global reference), and that the executable flight comes from some other 'local' call. Or they publish product.trajectory on /planning/initial_trajectory.
findings.proposed_name: (if ever renamed) computeDirectTrajectory, matching DirectPlanSettings/direct_trajectory_solver/RosPlanningBackend::planDirect
findings.reason: Real confusion, but computeGlobalTrajectory has 26 refs and planGlobalTraj 50 (mostly tests), and the 'GlobalTraj' log tags also appear in operator logs (path_manager.cpp:872-887,1241). A one-line doc stating that 'Global' = whole-mission direct solve and that product.trajectory is the execution trajectory resolves most of it. Revisit only if a deprecation cycle is planned anyway.
findings.affected_callers: computeGlobalTrajectory: non-test 16, test 10 (see above). planGlobalTraj: 0 production call sites, only comments/log strings (path_manager.cpp, replan_fsm.cpp:554,685,780, start_state.h 2, poly_traj_optimizer.h 1). 32 test refs (chain_experiment_test.cpp 28, committed_route_test.cpp 4).

findings.symbol: PathManager::planGlobalTraj (front_end_only flag and the parameter comment block)
findings.issue: planGlobalTraj is a pure compatibility entry with no production callers. Only line 151 calls it 'Compatibility entry' (no [[deprecated]] and no pointer to the replacement). With front_end_only=true it neither optimizes nor adopts and returns true. That duplicates planCommittedRoute (path_manager.cpp:1088-1095 vs 1065-1077). The 50-line comment at 59-108 documents planGlobalTraj/computeGlobalTrajectory parameters together with removed ones ('junction_head is gone', start_vel_synthesized_), so a reader cannot tell the current contract from the history.
findings.misreading_example: A new user sees `bool planGlobalTraj(..., bool front_end_only=false, ...)` and assumes true means a flight was planned and adopted. With front_end_only=true, executionTrajectory() still holds the previous flight.
findings.reason: Keep the name for the 32 test refs. Mark it legacy explicitly ('prefer computeGlobalTrajectory + applyPlanningComputation; front_end_only=true is equivalent to planCommittedRoute') and move the historical narrative out of the public header.
findings.affected_callers: front_end_only=true: 1 test call (committed_route_test.cpp:232-233, a legacy-equivalence check). planGlobalTraj overall: 0 production, 32 test.

findings.issue: The header says 'Returns patch id (>= 0) on success, -1 if SDF not built yet or out of map'. The implementation returns -2 (deferred, not an error) when the SDF does not exist yet (planning_environment_store.cpp:546-554). planning_environment_store.h:89, mission_planning_backend.h:24-25 and the FSM (replan_fsm.cpp:1325 counts -2 as deferred) all use -2.
findings.misreading_example: A caller trusting path_manager.h treats any negative return as rejection, or retries only on -1 waiting for the SDF. A -2 obstacle is then reported as rejected or double-queued.
findings.reason: A wrong doc on a public method; the fix is a one-line comment. The int return-code API could later become a typed result, but that is not needed now.
findings.affected_callers: PathManager::addDynamicSphere/Box: ros_planning_backend.cpp (initialize + forwarding), replan_fsm.cpp:1305,1312, path_manager.cpp flushPendingObstacles, plus tests.

findings.issue: The value is seconds INTO the trajectory (t0 in revalidateStoredTrajectory, path_manager.cpp:2099,2138; 0.0 in invalidateStoredTrajectoryForEnvChange, path_manager.cpp:2162). It is not a clock timestamp. The wire field it feeds is named detected_trajectory_time (TrajectoryExecutionControl.msg; replan_fsm.cpp:938,957). Next to it, PlannedTrajectory::start_time is absolute ROS seconds (planning_computation.h:21).
findings.misreading_example: A consumer of the observer event logs or compares event.detected_time against ROS now() (as with start_time) and gets nonsense, or adds trajectory start_time twice.
findings.proposed_name: detected_trajectory_time (field and revoke parameter)
findings.reason: This aligns with the existing wire name, removes a units/frame ambiguity, and has very few references.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test 5 (planning_execution.h:23,59; planning_execution.cpp:98,102; replan_fsm.cpp:938). Test 1 (planning_execution_test.cpp:123). Positional aggregate init at planning_execution.cpp:101 is unaffected.

findings.issue: SUSPECTED BEHAVIOUR MISMATCH (not naming; needs re-verification). The wire comment says the fields report 'Where the remaining flight was found to be blocked, and how far into the trajectory that is'. The code sends the blocked point `bad` together with t0, the time revalidation STARTED from (the current elapsed time), not the trajectory time at which `bad` lies. polylineClear returns only the point, so the hit time is never computed.
findings.misreading_example: An execution layer reads detected_trajectory_time as the time-to-impact location ('blocked 40 s ahead') and schedules recovery against it, but receives the current elapsed time, so the obstacle appears to be right now.
findings.reason: Either the msg comment or the code is wrong. Re-verify which meaning consumers (panel, execution layer, exec_abort_test.cpp) rely on before changing anything. This is separate from the detected_time rename.
findings.affected_callers: Producer path_manager.cpp:2138. Consumer replan_fsm.cpp:957. Test exec_abort_test.cpp (references the publish path).

findings.issue: The name says a generic environment change, but the implementation hard-codes ExecutionRevocationReason::POLICY_UNEVALUATED with a zero hit point. 'invalidate' also hides that it calls revoke, which notifies the observer, which publishes an ABORT on /planning/execution_control. The comment ('world changed in a way this node cannot re-judge') hints at the policy case only indirectly.
findings.misreading_example: A developer adding a 'map frame changed' trigger calls invalidateStoredTrajectoryForEnvChange(). Consumers then receive REASON_POLICY_UNEVALUATED ('zones changed') for a terrain/frame event.
findings.proposed_name: revokeForUnevaluatedZonePolicy() (or add an explicit ExecutionRevocationReason parameter)
findings.reason: One production caller and no tests make this nearly free. The current name invites misuse for other reasons, and the verb should match revoke.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test 1 call (replan_fsm.cpp:1457) + declaration/definition. Tests 0.

findings.issue: The comment above the new compute() entry opens with 'Same contract as planGlobalTraj: on true, path_manager->executionTrajectory() holds a flyable local trajectory'. That is false for compute, which never adopts and returns PlanningComputation, not bool. It also documents parameters that no longer exist (start_vel_synthesized, start_vel_commanded). The accurate contract only begins at line 75.
findings.misreading_example: A reader of the header assumes compute() leaves the chained result in executionTrajectory() and skips applyPlanningComputation, so the result is never executed.
findings.reason: This is the new public contract for the chain path. Move lines 43-74 to plan() or delete the stale parts. No rename needed.
findings.affected_callers: compute: ros_planning_backend.cpp:318, segment_chain_planner.cpp:258. Readers of the header.

findings.symbol: ReplanFSM public surface: timer_callback_group_, subscription_callback_group_, computeAndPublishPaths, globalTraj2ROSMsg, polyTraj2ROSMsg
findings.issue: The only explicit threading statement in this area is wrong. replan_fsm.h:100-104 says the timer has its own dedicated group and mentions a position_callback_group that does not exist. replan_fsm.cpp:314-322 deliberately places the 10 ms timer on subscription_callback_group_ to serialize it with planning (a data-race fix). timer_callback_group_ is public but never used. computeAndPublishPaths is the FSM tick (public, 0 external callers). globalTraj2ROSMsg has 0 callers and silently reads msg.trajectory_id as an INPUT (replan_fsm.cpp:512).
findings.misreading_example: An integrator adds a subscription on timer_callback_group_ believing the timer is isolated there, expecting it to run in parallel with planning. Or they call globalTraj2ROSMsg(fresh_msg) and get trajectory_id from uninitialized or zero input.
findings.reason: Fixing the header comment is essential because it misstates the serialization model. Optionally mark the unused group, the tick and globalTraj2ROSMsg as internal or deprecated. Renaming is not worth it; these are ROS-node internals exposed only because the class is public.
findings.affected_callers: timer_callback_group_/subscription_callback_group_: no use outside replan_fsm.cpp. computeAndPublishPaths: replan_fsm.cpp:322 (bind) only. polyTraj2ROSMsg: replan_fsm.cpp:992 + fsm_scenarios_test.cpp:346. globalTraj2ROSMsg: 0 callers.

findings.symbol: path_manager.h `using namespace ego_planner;` and replan_fsm.h FSM_LOG_* macros
findings.issue: Every header under include/ is installed, including ROS adapter and FSM headers. path_manager.h puts a namespace-scope using-directive into every includer (segment_chain_planner.h, replan_fsm.h, ros_planning_backend.cpp, consumers). replan_fsm.h defines unprefixed macros (FSM_LOG_INFO/WARN/ERROR/DEBUG) that expand to the members enable_debug_logs_, node_ and log_manager_ of whatever class the consumer is in. Nothing marks these as implementation details.
findings.misreading_example: A consumer including path_manager.h gets ego_planner::TailBoundary/LocalTrajData unqualified and later breaks when the directive is removed. Or a consumer that defines its own FSM_LOG_INFO gets a redefinition, or silently uses this one against its own members.
findings.reason: This is a boundary hygiene issue, not a rename. Removing the using-directive breaks unqualified uses (e.g. LocalTrajData at path_manager.h:148, replan_fsm.cpp:616). Document it now. Later, move the macros into replan_fsm.cpp (only log_visibility_test.cpp also uses them) and qualify the types.
findings.affected_callers: replan_fsm.h is included by replan_fsm.cpp, node.cpp, fsm_scenarios_test.cpp, log_visibility_test.cpp, unit_guard_test.cpp, mission_sequence_test.cpp. FSM_LOG_* is used in replan_fsm.cpp and log_visibility_test.cpp. path_manager.h is included transitively by most of the package.

findings.issue: Clearing terrain (an empty GridMap, i.e. clearTerrain()) also clears every dynamic obstacle and pending obstacle, and a geometry-changing terrain replacement clears all obstacles too (TerrainUpdate::obstacles_cleared). Neither clearTerrain(), setTerrain() nor setTerrainData() says so in its header. Only the TerrainUpdate struct field reveals it, and the value API (bool setTerrain / void clearTerrain) hides that struct.
findings.misreading_example: A facade user calls planner.clearTerrain(); planner.setTerrain(newCorridor) and expects the previously added obstacles to persist. They are gone.
findings.reason: This is the intended behaviour (obstacles were grounded on the old DEM), so the names are fine, but a destructive cross-resource effect belongs in the method comment of the public facade/backend.
findings.affected_callers: clearTerrain: mission_planner.cpp 1, ros_planning_backend.cpp 1, mission_planner_core_test.cpp 2, ros_planning_backend_test.cpp 1.

findings.issue: It sits next to bool setTerrain(TerrainGrid, std::string*) on the same class but returns void and discards the TerrainUpdate result, so rejection is invisible. PathManager::setTerrainData with the same name returns TerrainUpdate. The only difference between 'setTerrain' and 'setTerrainData' is the argument type and how failure is reported.
findings.misreading_example: A ROS caller uses backend->setTerrainData(msg) as the message-typed twin of setTerrain() and assumes it would signal failure. A malformed GridMap is silently ignored and planning proceeds on the old DEM.
findings.proposed_name: return TerrainUpdate (keep name); optional later rename ingestTerrainMessage
findings.reason: Changing void to TerrainUpdate is source-compatible for existing callers that ignore the result. A rename is optional.
findings.affected_callers: 2 test callers (route_search_backend_test.cpp:396, vehicle_model_injection_test.cpp:237). 0 production.

findings.issue: It returns a nullable pointer to the FIXED-WING TRANSITION parameters (model->fixedWingTransitionParameters()). It is null for other model families and when dynamics is off. PolyTrajOptimizer::dynamicsParams() (poly_traj_optimizer.h:591) has the same name but returns a const reference to the general dynamics parameters.
findings.misreading_example: A user with a non-fixed-wing VehicleModel calls pm->dynamicsParams() to read limits, gets nullptr, and concludes dynamics are disabled. segment_chain_planner.cpp:1557 actually relies on that null to refuse transitions.
findings.proposed_name: fixedWingTransitionParams()
findings.reason: The name hides the model-family restriction, and the same name in the optimizer has a different contract. Few callers, so the rename is cheap; keep the old name as a deprecated inline alias if desired.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test 3 (segment_chain_planner.cpp:1557,1560,1660). Test 4 (chain_experiment_test.cpp:813,1282,3852,3910).

findings.issue: It is declared const and named as a query, but it overwrites the mutable last_plan_.verdict/spans, which back lastFlightVerdict() and lastPhaseSpans(), and it emits log lines. A const method that mutates shared mutable state is also not safe to call concurrently, despite const suggesting so.
findings.misreading_example: A test or harness plans, then calls chain.evaluateFlight(candidate, spans, ...) to judge an alternative, then asserts on chain.lastFlightVerdict() expecting the PLAN's verdict, and gets the candidate's.
findings.reason: Document that it replaces the last-evaluation diagnostics. The ForTest twin is identical to the public method, so evaluateFlight could be made non-const or the twin dropped later. Not worth a rename.
findings.affected_callers: evaluateFlightForTest: chain_experiment_test.cpp 4. No production callers of the public member (internal code uses evaluateFlightInContext).

findings.issue: It sets legacy_transition_active_, which only planOverRoute reads (segment_chain_planner.cpp:2504). Every compute()/plan() silently resets it to false (segment_chain_planner.cpp:235). The name suggests a persistent mode switch for the planner.
findings.misreading_example: A coordinator calls setTransitionActive(true) and then plan(...). It expects the fallback-forbidden rule to apply, but plan() resets the flag and the single-shot fallback can run.
findings.proposed_name: setExplicitRouteTransitionActive (or document 'applies only to the next planOverRoute calls; reset by compute/plan')
findings.reason: Only 2 test callers. The field is already called legacy_*, so the public name should say it is scoped to the explicit-route seam.
findings.affected_callers: Test 2 (chain_experiment_test.cpp). Non-test 0.

findings.issue: It returns the LAST plan's confirmed (possibly auto-sized or merged) segment count (captureDiagnostics, segment_chain_planner.cpp:142), and before any plan the constructor's max(2, segments). It is not the configured count (that is RosPlanningBackend::configuredSegments()). Its siblings use the last* prefix (lastPhaseSpans, lastFlightVerdict, lastHeadPolicy).
findings.misreading_example: A caller reads chain.segments() to learn chain/segments from config and gets 5 after an auto-sized plan, while the config says 0 (auto).
findings.proposed_name: lastSegmentCount()
findings.reason: Test-only callers and consistency with the other last* accessors. Low priority; a doc comment is an acceptable alternative.
findings.affected_callers: Test 9 refs in chain_experiment_test.cpp (e.g. :743,:755,:1355). Non-test 0.

findings.issue: It binds a POINTER to the swarm (other aircraft) trajectory container into the member optimizer (setSwarmTrajs(&swarm_trajectories_)). It delivers neither our trajectory nor a copy. 'Traj' and 'deliver' hide both the subject (swarm) and the borrowing.
findings.misreading_example: A reader assumes it pushes the current planned trajectory into the optimizer as a warm start, and calls it after each plan expecting a better re-solve.
findings.proposed_name: bindSwarmTrajectoriesToOptimizer()
findings.reason: Few callers and it matches the existing bindRiskZonesToOptimizer naming. Low priority because the swarm path is legacy.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test 1 (ros_planning_backend.cpp:304). Test 4 (committed_route_test.cpp 1, chain_experiment_test.cpp 1, direct_plan_settings_test.cpp 2).

findings.issue: 'Now' actually means 'as measured by the LAST front-end search' (last_search_policy_). The methods return 0/false when nothing has been measured. They compute nothing about the current zones.
findings.misreading_example: After setRiskZonesRuntime(newZones) a caller reads zoneAvoidPassNow() expecting the pass the new zones require, but gets the previous search's pass.
findings.proposed_name: (optional) lastSearchZoneAvoidPass / lastSearchSuppressedCrossingExempt
findings.reason: A doc comment is enough. The call sites are few, but the names appear in [S13] logic where churn has a cost.
findings.affected_callers: zoneAvoidPassNow: non-test 2 (path_manager.cpp:2211,2253), test 5. suppressCrossingExemptNow: non-test 2 (path_manager.cpp:1646, segment_chain_planner.cpp:2659), test 0.

findings.issue: run_parallel only selects a word in a log line (segment_chain_planner.cpp:1966,1969) and has no effect on the committed route. 'commit' does not touch execution, but it does advance the policy epoch and rewrite PathManager's compatibility route accessors through planCommittedRoute.
findings.misreading_example: A caller passes run_parallel=true expecting the front end to run in parallel, or expecting the route to be prepared differently for a parallel solve.

findings.affected_callers: Non-test 3 (segment_chain_planner.cpp), test 5 (chain_experiment_test.cpp).

findings.issue: identityCounter() returns the LAST issued trajectory_id (adoptCurrent pre-increments: current_.traj_id = ++next_identity_). The private member is nevertheless named next_identity_. The public name is neutral but undocumented.

findings.issue: The environment owner lives in planning_environment_store.h, but the execution owner lives in planning_execution.h, while planning_environment.h is the value input patch. Both stores are installed headers, yet they are reachable only as PathManager's private members (path_manager.h:642,645) and dedicated tests. replan_fsm.h:126-128 calls them 'private environment and execution owners'. Nothing marks them internal or unstable.

findings.issue: 'calculations' also contains the MissionPlanner facade (src/mission_planner.cpp) and the stateful execution owner (src/planning_execution.cpp). The CMake comment at 55-59 says this but the name does not. '_lib' does not say it is the ROS adapter + FSM + PathManager target, and it is the only target that offers a concrete backend (RosPlanningBackend), which is why library_consumer links mission_planner_client to path_manager_lib.

findings.issue: It adopts a zero-velocity min-jerk hold into the execution slot (consumes a trajectory ID via adoptEmergencyTrajectory), clears and republishes viz, and logs a WARN. It does NOT publish the trajectory to /planning/trajectory (the FSM does that via callEmergencyStop + polyTraj2ROSMsg, replan_fsm.cpp:988-992). The message doc notes that a zero-velocity hold is not flyable for the fixed-wing platform.
findings.misreading_example: A library user calls pm->EmergencyStop(pos) and assumes the vehicle has been commanded to stop.
findings.reason: This is a legacy, FSM-only path (planning_execution.h:49-50 already says 'legacy emergency command'). A rename is not worth it. State 'replaces the execution slot only; the caller must publish'.
findings.affected_callers: Non-test: replan_fsm.cpp:989 (1 call). Test: terrain_risk_mask_test.cpp 2.

findings.issue: The field is called 'generation' but holds the composite environmentRevision() (= zone generation + terrain generation + SDF revision, planning_environment_store.h:111-113). Sibling 'generation' accessors (zoneGeneration, zonePolicyGeneration, TerrainData::generation) are single-component counters.
findings.misreading_example: A user compares result.environment_generation with pm->zonePolicyGeneration() to decide whether zones changed since the plan, and gets an always-different or false-equal answer.
findings.reason: The wire field TrajectoryExecutionControl.environment_generation fixes the name. A one-line note 'equals PathManager::environmentRevision(); identity only' at each declaration is enough. finding.issue: applied==true means 'the computation was accepted and its context consumed', NOT 'a trajectory was adopted'. An accepted no-product failure, or a refusal that only invalidates, returns {true, current_.traj_id, drone_id}, where current_.traj_id is the PREVIOUS (possibly just-invalidated) flight's ID. The header has no comment on this. Only docs/design/planning_computation_usage_ko.md:79-80 shows that hasTrajectory() must be checked after applied.
finding.misreading_example: A new caller writes `auto r = mgr->applyPlanningComputation(c); if (r.applied) publish(c.product->trajectory, r.trajectory_id);`. For an accepted failure, product may be absent (crash), or the post-gate rejected intermediate product may be present (product kept for legacy ID effects), and it gets published under the old flight's ID.
finding.proposed_name: keep `applied`; add a doc comment, and optionally an additive `bool adopted_trajectory` (true only when a product was adopted)
finding.reason: The name is defensible (the effect was applied), but the struct is the public outcome of the new compute->apply contract and its two failure semantics are invisible at the declaration. An additive field is cheap. Renaming `applied` would touch about 40 sites for no gain.
finding.affected_callers: Receipt `.applied` reads: non-test 7 (ros_planning_backend.cpp:221; path_manager.cpp:1104,1118,1774; segment_chain_planner.cpp:259,2526 and 3133 via apply). Tests: planning_execution_test.cpp 18, execution_adoption_test.cpp 10, chain_experiment_test.cpp 3, committed_route_test.cpp 1. The design doc example is planning_computation_usage_ko.md:77-80.

verdict.evidence:
The behaviour claim holds. planning_execution.cpp:66 says `++revision_;  // Accepted no-product failures also consume their context.`, and :80 returns `{true, current_.traj_id, current_.drone_id}` whether or not a product was adopted. On a no-product failure, current_.traj_id is unchanged, so it is the previous flight's ID, or 0 if no flight has been adopted yet. On a refusal with invalidate_execution set, :67-78 first adopts the rejected intermediate product, which gives it a new ID, and :79 then invalidates it. So in that case trajectory_id is the ID of the just-invalidated rejected product, not the old flight's ID. The finding states this case inaccurately.

The struct at planning_computation.h:57-61 has no comment, which is also true. But the confusion is already guarded at the places a caller passes through. (a) PlanningComputation::product, planning_computation.h:30-32: "It is NOT a flyable result: consumers must use hasTrajectory()". (b) path_manager.h:141-143, above `applyPlanningComputation`: "Rejects foreign, stale or previously applied computations with no mutation. An accepted failure may explicitly invalidate execution." (c) ros_planning_backend.h:58 marks `executionManager()` as "Execution/callback adapter access only, absent from MissionPlanner's API", so the receipt is reachable only through the adapter, not the MissionPlanner public surface. (d) docs/design/planning_computation_usage_ko.md:46 and :79-80 show `applied` and then `hasTrajectory()`.

Every production caller handles it correctly. ros_planning_backend.cpp:221 checks `!receipt.applied`, :229 returns early on `!result.status.hasTrajectory()`, and only then does :237 copy `receipt.trajectory_id`. The other callers (path_manager.cpp:1104, 1119, 1773; segment_chain_planner.cpp:259, 2522) use `.applied` only as a staleness or adoption gate, and their returned PlanResult carries the success or failure.

In the misreading example, the `c.product->trajectory` dereference is the very thing comment (a) forbids. The part that is really hidden at a declaration is the meaning of `trajectory_id` on failure.
caller_examples: mmp_path_planning/src/path_manager/src/ros_planning_backend.cpp:221 (if (!receipt.applied)) and :237 (result.trajectory_id = receipt.trajectory_id, gated by hasTrajectory at :229)
verdict.note:
Keep the names `applied` and `trajectory_id`. Renaming would change 6 production `.applied` reads plus about 32 test reads for no gain.

Fix: add a doc comment above `struct ExecutionReceipt` (planning_computation.h:57). It should say that `applied` means "this computation's effects were accepted and its context consumed; it does not mean a new flight was adopted, so check PlanningComputation::hasTrajectory()". It should also say that `trajectory_id` and `drone_id` describe the execution slot after apply. That ID can be 0, the previous flight's ID, or a just-invalidated rejected product's ID. It names a new flight only when hasTrajectory() is true.

I do not recommend the additive `bool adopted_trajectory`. It duplicates computed.hasTrajectory(), adds a second source of truth, and would be true for the invalidated intermediate product unless defined carefully. The struct is reachable only via the adapter-only executionManager().

verdict.evidence:
Holds up: h:59 `std::shared_ptr<PathManager> executionManager() const` returns the full mutable manager, and the FSM uses it to change the environment: replan_fsm.cpp:1227 `setTerrainData`, :1235 `revalidateAfterEnvChange`, :1295-1312 `clearDynamicObstacles`/`addDynamicBox`/`addDynamicSphere`, :1436 `setRiskZonesRuntime`. The header has `compute()` (h:41) but no backend `apply`, and `plan()` calls `manager_->applyPlanningComputation` internally (cpp:215-217). The documented compute->adopt recipe therefore has to go through `backend->executionManager()->applyPlanningComputation(computed)` (planning_computation_usage_ko.md:77-78).

Factually wrong: (1) The claim that calls "skip requireInitialized()". `executionManager()` runs `requireInitialized()` itself (cpp:140), and nothing ever sets `initialized_` back to false, so a pointer obtained this way always refers to an initialized manager. (2) The claim that calls bypass "backend validation". The backend's environment setters forward straight to the manager with no extra checks: `setTerrainData` -> `manager_->setTerrainData` (cpp:176-180), `setRiskZones` -> `manager_->setRiskZonesRuntime` (cpp:181-184), and `addDynamicSphere`/`addDynamicBox` (cpp:185-193). `encodeTerrainGrid` (cpp:165) only converts the ROS-free `TerrainGrid` value input, which the FSM does not use (it receives a GridMap). The FSM also needs the update result returned at :1227, and the backend's `setTerrainData` (cpp:176) returns void. Going through the manager is therefore required, not a bypass.

Existing docs already address the "narrow facade" misreading. planning_library_usage_ko.md:106-108 says it is "not a separate planner but a shared reference to the same `PathManager` the backend uses". modularized_function_api_ko.md:80-81 limits it to the existing FSM/execution adapter, and replan_fsm.cpp:170-171 says "Keep a manager alias for the existing ROS execution/environment callbacks". Only the header comment at h:58, "Execution/callback adapter access only", fails to say that the pointer is the shared, mutable, full `PathManager`. A reader who sees only the header could take the misreading example at face value.

Revised recommendation:
1. Primary fix (document): change the comment at ros_planning_backend.h:58. It should say this returns the backend's shared, mutable `PathManager`. That includes environment mutation (terrain, risk zones, obstacles, revalidation) and execution adoption via `applyPlanningComputation`. It is not a narrowed facade, and it is meant only for the existing FSM/ROS execution adapter.
2. Optional, additive: add `ExecutionReceipt RosPlanningBackend::apply(const PlanningComputation&)`, forwarding to `manager_->applyPlanningComputation`. This would let the compute()/apply pair stay on the backend, and the usage doc at :77-78 could use it. Do this only if the team wants compute() callers to stop needing the PathManager pointer. It is an API nicety, not a contract defect. The token/context checks already reject stale or foreign adoption (execution_adoption_test.cpp:227 exercises the foreign manager).
3. Rename to `legacyPathManager()`: not recommended. "legacy" would be inaccurate, because this pointer is the live path the current FSM uses. The old name `legacyManager()` was deliberately retired (incremental_modularization_ko.md:926, README.md:79), so reusing it would add confusion. The rename would touch 1 production caller, 14 test lines, the SFINAE trait at execution_adoption_test.cpp:39, 5 docs and the SVG, for little benefit.

verdict.note: The claim holds on the facts. The name does not say "relative to trajectory start", the existing comments do not say it either, and the nearby `start_time` fields (LocalTrajData, PlannedTrajectory) are absolute ROS seconds, so the misreading is plausible. The rename is very cheap: a grep of src excluding reports/experiments gives 2 definition sites in the header, 3 non-test uses (planning_execution.cpp:98,102; replan_fsm.cpp:938) and 1 test use (planning_execution_test.cpp:123). I lowered the priority from medium to low for three reasons: (a) it is diagnostic only, and the msg says "the decision is `action`, not these"; (b) the only in-tree observer (ReplanFSM) already maps it correctly; (c) a one-line doc comment would remove most of the risk on its own. Extra contract point to document alongside it (this is not a bug): for POLICY_UNEVALUATED, path_manager.cpp:2162-2163 passes 0.0 and a zero hit as placeholders meaning "no point was detected". A reader could take that as "detected at the trajectory start". Also, t0 is clamped to [0, duration] (path_manager.cpp:2101), so 0.0 can be either a real value or a placeholder. Recommended comment: "seconds since this trajectory's start_time at which the blocked remainder begins; 0 with hit=Zero when no point was detected (POLICY_UNEVALUATED)".

finding.issue: SUSPECTED BEHAVIOUR MISMATCH (not naming; needs re-verification). The wire comment says the fields report 'Where the remaining flight was found to be blocked, and how far into the trajectory that is'. The code sends the blocked point `bad` together with t0, the time revalidation STARTED from (the current elapsed time), not the trajectory time at which `bad` lies. polylineClear returns only the point, so the hit time is never computed.

verdict.evidence: The mismatch is real. The msg comment at TrajectoryExecutionControl.msg:38-39 says "Where the remaining flight was found to be blocked, and how far into the trajectory that is." The producer does not do that. path_manager.cpp:2102 sets `t0 = std::clamp(t_from, 0.0, lt.duration)`. :2125 calls `searcher_.polylineClear(pts, &bad)`, which returns only the point, and the sample index/time of `bad` is thrown away. :2138 then calls `execution_->revoke(reason, bad, t0, environmentRevision())`, so the time sent is where the check started, not where the hit is. t_from is elapsed time "now": path_manager.cpp:2172-2176 and replan_fsm.cpp:1343-1347 compute `t_cur = now - start_time`. The value goes through planning_execution.cpp:96-103 (`ExecutionRevocation{..., hit, detected_time}`, defined in planning_execution.h:17-24, `double detected_time`, no comment) into replan_fsm.cpp:938/956 `msg.detected_trajectory_time = t_detected`. The POLICY_UNEVALUATED path, path_manager.cpp:2162-2163, sends `Eigen::Vector3d::Zero(), 0.0`, and the msg does not document this sentinel. The header doc for revalidateStoredTrajectory (path_manager.h:410-436) describes t_from as "seconds into it" and says nothing about what is reported. The log at replan_fsm.cpp:957-962 prints "withdrawn ... at t=%.2f s, point (...)", which fits detection time but not the wire comment. What weakens the finding: nothing reads the field. The only TrajectoryExecutionControl subscriber, mmp_vehicle_dynamics/src/dynamics_sim_node.cpp:77-79/216-219, never mentions `detected`, and exec_abort_test.cpp has no `detected` references. The msg itself says the field is diagnostic: "the decision is `action`, not these" (msg:39). So the misreading example (an execution layer scheduling recovery from it) is plausible for a new third-party consumer reading the msg, but no current code is affected.

I confirmed this by reading the code, so no runtime check is needed. Lowered from medium to low for three reasons: (1) no consumer in the tree reads detected_trajectory_time or detected_point (0 readers; only the producer at replan_fsm.cpp:953-956 and docs/exec_cancel_layer.md:43-44 mention them); (2) the msg marks these fields as diagnostic only; (3) changing the meaning or fixing the comment does not change the wire type. Two ways to fix it, for the team to choose: (a) document-only: change msg:38-39 and add a comment on planning_execution.h:23 saying it is "trajectory time [s] from which the remainder was re-checked (≈ elapsed time at detection); 0 and zero point for REASON_POLICY_UNEVALUATED"; (b) behaviour fix: report the hit time as well, which needs polylineClear to return the sample index (the time is t0+(dur-t0)*k/n). verdict.evidence: Header doc path_manager.h:453-454 says only "Drop the stored trajectory because the world changed in a way this node cannot re-judge. Same two fields every other refusal zeroes." It does not mention risk zones, the POLICY_UNEVALUATED reason, the revocation observer or the ABORT. The second sentence looks stale, because the body no longer zeroes fields directly. The impl at path_manager.cpp:2162-2163 calls `execution_->revoke(EnvChangeReason::POLICY_UNEVALUATED, Eigen::Vector3d::Zero(), 0.0, environmentRevision())` and then `clearTrajectoryViz()`, so the reason is hard-coded. Its sibling methods take the reason as a parameter: `revalidateStoredTrajectory(..., EnvChangeReason reason)` at path_manager.h:435-436 and `revalidateAfterEnvChange(const char*, EnvChangeReason)` at path_manager.h:452. That makes the reason-less "ForEnvChange" name inconsistent with them. review.area_summary:
F1 (simulation engine + ROS-independent Python map loading) is in reasonably good naming shape. Most public names show units (_m, _mps, _s, _u), ownership (takeResult() &&, owned SimulationInput/SimulationResult, a newly allocated elevation_u) and side effects (resolve_map_mission/load_map docstrings say what they read). I do not recommend a broad rename. Findings fall into four groups:

(1) Frame/axis contract (highest value): point_mass_eom.hpp:12 calls the frame "mission ENU", but [TERRAIN-FRAME] (frame.py:59-64) is +x NORTH, +y WEST, z up. So heading_rad is measured from north toward west, not compass and not ENU yaw. elevation_u[0,0] is the max-x/max-y (north-west) corner, not min_bound_u. These need doc fixes, not renames.

(2) Two narrow, low-cost rename candidates in the C++ simulation API: SimulationSession::controller(t,state), which returns a realized control yet shares its name with the SimulationInput::controller strategy field (1 test caller), and SimulationMetrics::violation_steps, which is really an envelope-violation count; path_manager already uses env_violation_steps (1 node and 3 test references).

(3) Python map API vocabulary: the word "mission" names three shapes (mission.Mission, ResolvedMapMission exposed as MapLoadResult.mission, and the ResolvedMission ROS msg), which forces result.mission.mission. normalize_elevation returns a MapLoadResult, masks <=0 m to NaN and takes a unitless actual_cell_size. vrt_resolution/full_map_override hide unit/type/None-vs-'' semantics. Document first; renames only with aliases.

(4) Doc drift: the mmp_vehicle_dynamics/__init__.py docstring cites a stale config value and a non-existent mmp_dynamics_sim package. A comment on SimulationReference belongs to PolynomialReference. load_anchor is a compat wrapper with 0 callers whose docstring names a caller that does not use it.

One suspected (minor) bug: parameters_from_ros uses `or 100.0`, which silently replaces 0 for the frame units. It needs re-verification.

Boundary: all 5 vehicle_dynamics headers are installed via install(DIRECTORY include/). trajectory_abort_state.hpp is an execution-protocol helper that lives in the dynamics package, and path_manager's test uses it. mmp_terrain/__init__.py is empty, so public vs ROS-bound modules are separated only by module name (ros_terrain, terrain_publisher). The Python simulation API is intentionally not bound (README:180).

vocabulary_notes: Frame axes: point_mass_eom.hpp:12 says 'mission ENU'. frame.py:59-64 and terrain_data.h:13-14 define [TERRAIN-FRAME] as +x north, +y west (mirrored grid). mission.py:9 says 'wx tracks northing, wy tracks easting'. 'ENU' appears nowhere else in vehicle_dynamics/path_manager headers, so the EOM comment is the outlier.

Frame unit (100 m) has three names: TARGET_CELL_SIZE_M (frame.py:86; 21 refs in 6 files), FrameUnits.xy_m/z_m (mmp_vehicle_dynamics/__init__.py:43-46), and PolynomialReference::unit_xy_m/unit_z_m (trajectory_simulation.hpp:24). The terrain one is a hard constant; the dynamics one is configured from optimization/dynamics_unit_*_m.

Mission has three shapes under one word: mission.Mission (mission.py:49; start=[wx_u, wy_u, z_m_AGL]); ResolvedMapMission namedtuple, exposed as MapLoadResult.mission (map_loader.py:79,97) and passed as mission_snapshot= (map_loader.py:507), with internal aliases ctx (map_loader.py:199) and _Resolved (terrain_publisher.py:341); and the mmp_mission_msgs ResolvedMission msg (response.mission, terrain_publisher.py:376; mission.py:218). The sha field is mission_sha in Python (map_loader.py:80) and mission_sha256 in the msg (terrain_publisher.py:396).

Anchor raster path has four names: full_map_override (MapLoadInput, map_loader.py:59), full_map_path (local, map_loader.py:138), anchor_path (ResolvedMapMission, map_loader.py:80), and source_paths[0] (map_loader.py:388).

Envelope check verbs: SimulationMotionModel::audit / SimulationEnvelopeReading (trajectory_simulation.hpp:95,50), evaluateInverseDynamics/isWithinEnvelope (flight_dynamics), and path_manager flight_evaluation/flight_evaluator. 'audit' is used only in the simulation API.
Envelope-violation counter: SimulationMetrics::violation_steps (trajectory_simulation.hpp:131) vs WaypointEval env_violation_steps (waypoint_eval.h:341) for the same isWithinEnvelope==false count.

Duration: SimulationSession::totalDuration() (trajectory_simulation.hpp:159) == SimulationResult::reference_duration_s (hpp:136) == PolynomialReference::totalDuration() (hpp:25). This matches PolyTraj::totalDuration in mmp_traj_utils/poly_traj.hpp, so the project vocabulary is consistent.

Control inputs: PointMassInputs {thrust_n, lift_n, drag_n, bank_rad} (point_mass_eom.hpp:53-59) vs SimulationControl {thrust_n, lift_n, bank_rad, drag_n} (trajectory_simulation.hpp:47). Same quantities, different declaration order.

Elevation: C++ TerrainData::elevation (terrain_data.h:25, unit implicit) vs Python MapLoadResult.elevation_u (map_loader.py:93, explicit u). Both are absolute elevation / 100 m, while mission z is metres AGL (mission.py:23).

The simulation position also carries absolute altitude (planner z * unit_z_m), not AGL (README.md:143). No other vehicle_dynamics/path_manager header uses ENU.

finding.issue: The installed EOM header says the position is in 'mission ENU'. The planner/terrain frame is [TERRAIN-FRAME]: +x NORTH, +y WEST, z up (frame.py:59-64; terrain_data.h:13-14). The simulation position also carries absolute altitude (planner z * unit_z_m), not AGL (README.md:143). No other vehicle_dynamics/path_manager header uses ENU.
finding.misreading_example: An external simulator author treats SimulationState::position_m.x() as east and heading_rad=0 as 'pointing east'. Their aircraft then flies 90 degrees off and mirrored relative to the planner/RViz.
finding.reason: The math is frame-agnostic (any right-handed z-up frame), so no symbol needs renaming. Only the comment is wrong. Replace it with 'planner frame metres: +x north, +y west, z up (absolute altitude, not AGL); see mmp_terrain/frame.py [TERRAIN-FRAME]'.
finding.affected_callers: Comment only; 0 code callers. The frame convention affects PointMassState/SimulationState consumers: dynamics_sim_node.cpp:334-338, trajectory_simulation.cpp, trajectory_simulation_test.cpp.

verdict.evidence: The comment is wrong. point_mass_eom.hpp:12 reads "State:  position [m, mission ENU]", and posdot = V[cos g cos psi, cos g sin psi, sin g] (point_mass_eom.hpp:19, pointMassVelocity :69-75) makes heading 0 point along +x. The planner frame is defined in mmp_terrain/mmp_terrain/frame.py:24-28 ("frame +x points NORTH and frame +y points WEST") and path_manager/include/path_manager/terrain_data.h:13-15 ([TERRAIN-FRAME] mirrored row/col mapping). Real consumers feed planner-frame metres straight in, with no ENU conversion: trajectory_simulation.cpp:87-95 (simulationPointMassState copies position_m and heading_rad unchanged), and dynamics_sim_node.cpp:338-347 (setRPY(bank, -gamma, heading_rad) as the yaw, then position_m.cwiseQuotient(frameScale()) published with frame_id "map", where frameScale = (unit_xy_m, unit_xy_m, unit_z_m) at :184-187). The neighbouring header trajectory_simulation.hpp:11-14 already says "existing planner frame", so the two installed headers contradict each other. z is altitude, not AGL (mmp_vehicle_dynamics/README.md:143). A grep for ENU across src (reports/experiments excluded) finds it only at point_mass_eom.hpp:12 and in the Korean design note mmp_path_planning/docs/transition_v1_test_design.md:68-69 ("미션 ENU에서 적분"), which is the probable origin of the wording. The header is installed (CMakeLists.txt:47 install(DIRECTORY include/)). Overstatement in the finding: planner (+x N, +y W, z up) and ENU are both right-handed and z-up (N x W = Up), so they differ by a pure 90 deg yaw rotation, NOT a mirror. heading_rad is counter-clockwise from +x in both, so the misreading gives a 90 deg heading/position offset with no mirroring.
caller_examples: mmp_vehicle_dynamics/src/dynamics_sim_node.cpp:338-342 heading_rad used as map-frame yaw, position_m divided by frameScale
verdict.note: The factual claim holds: "mission ENU" contradicts the [TERRAIN-FRAME] planner frame that every real caller uses. It also contradicts the sibling installed header trajectory_simulation.hpp:11, which says "planner frame". A comment-only fix is enough. No symbol rename and no behaviour change are needed, and the EOM math does not depend on the frame (any right-handed z-up frame works). I downgraded it from high/contract_issue to medium/document for three reasons. (1) It is a one-line comment fix with no API impact. (2) All 45 production and 24 test references are in this repo and already use the planner frame correctly; no external consumer or example depends on ENU. (3) The misreading example is overstated: the frames differ by a 90 deg yaw rotation, not a mirror. Suggested wording: "position [m, planner frame: +x north, +y west, z up = altitude (not AGL); see mmp_terrain/frame.py [TERRAIN-FRAME]]; heading psi CCW from +x". Optionally also fix docs/transition_v1_test_design.md:69 ("미션 ENU"). Counts are line-level matches for PointMassState|pointMassVelocity|pointMassDerivative|point_mass_eom outside the defining header, excluding docs/ and docs/validation. "Tests" means files under /test/ (point_mass_eom_test.cpp: 15, transition_experiment_test.cpp: 9).

finding.issue: The method is a noun and has the same name as SimulationInput::controller (hpp:125), which holds the TrackingController strategy. It does not return the controller: it samples the reference, runs the controller AND model->realize(), and returns the realized SimulationControl (trajectory_simulation.cpp:269-275).
finding.misreading_example: `auto c = session.controller(t, s);` reads as getting the controller object, or as getting the raw commanded acceleration. It actually returns saturated, realized forces/bank, and acceleration_mps2 includes gravity.
finding.reason: High confusion, very low cost: 1 external test caller, no node caller (the node gets the same value via derivative(..., &applied) at dynamics_sim_node.cpp:335), and 2 internal call sites. Do it now, before external users appear.
finding.affected_callers: rg 'controller(' over the engine: trajectory_simulation.cpp:269 (definition), :279 (derivative), :325 (integrateRk4); test: trajectory_simulation_test.cpp:152 (1). Docs: transition_phase_contract.md has 1 unrelated match. No other packages.

verdict.evidence: The header doc does not clear up the confusion. The only nearby comment is hpp:161 "// Playback uses the same controller/model arithmetic as integration.", and it covers sampleReference/stateVelocity/controller/derivative as a group. It never says that `controller()` returns a realized control. Name collision: the same header declares `TrackingController::Ptr controller;` as a field of SimulationInput (hpp:125). That field is set via `input.controller = ...` in trajectory_simulation_example.cpp:20, dynamics_sim_node.cpp:278 and README.md:167, so for users `controller` already means "the strategy object". Implementation at cpp:269-275: it samples the reference (sampleReference), gets the model velocity, calls `input_.controller->commandedAcceleration(...)`, then returns `input_.model->realize(state, command)`. So it is sample + command + realize, not a getter. Gravity claim: FixedWingMotionModel::realize sets `control.acceleration_mps2 = gravity + ...` (cpp:143, cpp:188), so the returned acceleration is the total realized acceleration with gravity included, not the commanded acceleration. The misreading example is plausible: `auto c = session.controller(t, s)` reads as a getter, and a reader could also take `c.acceleration_mps2` to be the command. References (rg '\bcontroller\s*\(' over src, reports/experiments excluded): 1 declaration (hpp:164), 1 definition (cpp:269), 2 internal callers (cpp:279 in derivative(), cpp:325 in integrateRk4 for bank_rad), 1 test caller (test/trajectory_simulation_test.cpp:152). No production or example caller outside the engine. The node gets the value through `simulation_->derivative(state.time_s, state, &applied)` (dynamics_sim_node.cpp:335). No Python binding, no README use of the method. The doc match at src/mmp_path_planning/docs/transition_phase_contract.md:277 is a prose mention of an old node-private structure (it cites dynamics_sim_node.cpp:359 integrateRk4, which now lives in trajectory_simulation.cpp:298), so that doc is stale either way.
verdict.note: Confirmed. The finding's facts hold, and the doc comment does not settle the ambiguity. Renaming is cheap: 2 internal call sites, 1 test, no node, example, binding or README use. On the proposed name: `controlAt` is better, but it still does not say "realized". `realizedControlAt(time_s, state)` (or `realizedControl`) matches the realize() vocabulary used in the strategy interface (hpp:83-91), so it would be clearer. Keeping a [[deprecated]] inline forwarder named `controller` is optional. The API was introduced in a recent commit and has no known external users, so a straight rename plus a one-line doc comment ("samples reference, runs TrackingController, returns model->realize() result; acceleration_mps2 is total incl. gravity") is acceptable. If the team prefers no rename, the minimum fix is that doc comment at hpp:164. Separate doc-staleness item (not a rename): transition_phase_contract.md:275-279 still describes integrateRk4 as a node-private member at dynamics_sim_node.cpp:359. It now lives in SimulationSession::integrateRk4 (trajectory_simulation.cpp:298), so that statement needs re-checking. No behavioural bug is suspected here.

finding.issue: elevation_u is absolute elevation (MSL) divided by 100, while mission z is metres AGL (mission.py:23). Index [0,0] is the raster north-west cell, which is the frame (max x, max y) corner: row 0 = north = x max, col 0 = west = y max (frame.py:59-62; terrain_data.h:13-14). It is not min_bound_u. The module docstring says 'row zero north' and 'rows span X' but never states that index 0 is at max_bound_u.
finding.misreading_example: A Python consumer computes the world position of elevation_u[i,j] as min_bound_u + (i+0.5, j+0.5)*resolution_u, which mirrors the terrain on both axes. Or they compare elevation_u*100 with mission z directly as if both were AGL.
finding.reason: The name and units are right; the indexing/datum contract is only implicit. Add the explicit formula (wx = max_bound_u[0] - (row+0.5)*resolution_u, wy = max_bound_u[1] - (col+0.5)*resolution_u, matching terrain_data.h:13-14) and the 'MSL, not AGL' note.
finding.affected_callers: to_grid_map (ros_terrain.py:20-33); any external Python consumer (examples print shape only).

verdict.evidence: Facts check out. map_loader.py:9-11 (module docstring) says "Native raster order is retained (row zero north, column zero west). Grid rows span frame X and columns span frame Y; all X/Y/Z grid units are 100 metres. Mission Z remains metres AGL". The class docstring map_loader.py:86-91 covers only ownership and allocation, not orientation or datum. frame.py:25-28 says "wx is Lx at row 0 (the north edge)... wy is Ly at column 0 (the west edge)... frame +x points NORTH and frame +y points WEST", and en_to_frame at frame.py:220-223 agrees. So index [0,0] is the (max_bound_u[0], max_bound_u[1]) corner. terrain_data.h:13-15 gives the mirrored formula wx = origin_x + length_x - (row+0.5)*res. map_loader.py:500 sets `elevation_scaled = elevation / TARGET_CELL_SIZE_M`, which is the raw DEM value / 100, and values <-9000 are set to NaN at :488. Nothing says that value is absolute height and not AGL. The words "MSL"/"AMSL" do not appear anywhere in mmp_terrain or the path_manager headers. Also, mission.py:23 says only that `z` is metres AGL. The docs file map_loader_api_ko.md:16,33-37 repeats "행 0 북쪽, 열 0 서쪽" (row 0 north, column 0 west), "height_u * 100 = metres" and "미션의 Z는 ... metres AGL" (mission Z is metres AGL). It never says that index 0 maps to max_bound_u, or that X grows northward.
caller_examples: src/mmp_terrain/mmp_terrain/ros_terrain.py:32 (flatten(order='F') -> GridMap, orientation handled by C++ terrain_data.h mirror)
verdict.note: No test directories under src/ reference elevation_u. The 17 test references are outside src/: map/test_map_loader.py (16) and map/test_map_loader_ros.py:27. The finding is accurate, but the fix is documentation only and the impact is small. In production, the only consumer that reads cell positions is ros_terrain.to_grid_map. It passes the array through in column-major order, and the C++ side applies the mirror in terrain_data.h:13-15. No Python production code computes positions from indices, and the example prints shape/dtype only. A new Python user is still plausibly misled: the dataclass puts `min_bound_u` beside `elevation_u`, so the min-origin formula looks natural, and frame.py:25-28 (which states the mirror) is never cross-referenced from map_loader. The datum point is weaker than the finding claims. The module docstring already sets "Mission Z remains metres AGL" against the grid Z unit. "MSL" is an unverified label: the code shows only that the value is the raw DEM value / 100. Wording should say "absolute DEM height (not AGL)" unless the DEM's vertical datum is confirmed. Recommended fix: two sentences added to the MapLoadResult docstring and map_loader_api_ko.md. The first gives elevation_u[r,c] centre wx = max_bound_u[0] - (r+0.5)*resolution_u, wy = max_bound_u[1] - (c+0.5)*resolution_u, i.e. [0,0] = max-bound corner, and points to frame.py. The second says values are absolute DEM height / 100, unlike mission z (AGL). No rename (elevation_u is accurate) and no contract change.

Unit-suffix convention is applied unevenly: newer APIs suffix units (pos_u/vel_u, position_m, speed_mps, resolution_m, elevation_u, min_bound_u) but TerrainGrid::resolution/center_x/length_x/elevation (planning_environment.h:19-25), RiskSettings fields (step, agl, slice_offset, heatmap_agl_max) and FlightPhaseMetrics::min_agl (flight_evaluator.h:82) are planner units without a suffix. Python MapLoadResult::resolution_u == C++ TerrainGrid::resolution; resolution_m is metres.

ros_ file prefix is not a reliable ROS-dependency marker: ROS-typed headers without it: planning_visualization_data.h:8-13, direct_plan_settings.h:3 (rclcpp::Parameter), trajectory_message.h:7, planning_environment_store.h:8, replan_fsm.h:4-20, path_manager.h:4, segment_chain_planner.h:11; ros_route_search.h:3 and ros_terrain_grid.h:6 do follow it. builtin_route_search.h is ROS-free but implemented only in path_manager_lib.

CMake target naming has two patterns: <pkg>_lib (path_manager_lib, path_optimizer_lib, path_planner_lib) vs capability name (path_manager_calculations, path_planner_sdf) vs bare package name (mmp_vehicle_dynamics::mmp_vehicle_dynamics). No ALIAS targets exist anywhere in the workspace (grep).

Package/word 'planner': package path_planner = A*/FM2/SDF front-end search library (path_planner/CMakeLists.txt:44-77), class MissionPlanner/target path_manager_* = whole-mission planner, PathManager = ROS node adapter, path_optimizer = MINCO solver. A new user will assume `path_planner` plans missions.

'obstacle_clearance' means different things by context: optimizer SDF penalty onset (optimizer_params.yaml:249), front-end blocked threshold (yaml:230), terrain floor offset in RiskSettings/terrain_risk.cpp:153, AGL band in FlightEvaluationSettings (flight_evaluator.h:22, flight_evaluator.cpp:98). In planning_visualization_data.h the word `Obstacle` (h:68) means a dynamic obstacle while RiskSettings::obstacle_clearance (h:59) is a terrain-relative floor, in the same header.

Legacy namespaces visible in the new public API: ego_planner:: (146 lines / 27 files, e.g. ego_planner::TailBoundary in mission_planner_example.cpp:52), swarm_formation:: (39 lines / 17 files; LogManager in ros_planning_backend.h:9,30), poly_traj:: ; new namespaces are path_manager:: / path_manager::visualization / mmp_vehicle_dynamics::.
Header guard/style (pragma once vs #ifndef) differs across headers; deliberately NOT reported as a finding (style).

findings.symbol: all make*() messages: frame_id "map" with planner-unit coordinates (no frame/unit statement in the header)
findings.issue: Every message is hard-coded to frame "map" (cpp:62,84,138,161,192,233,241,268,306,569,795,819,1189,1199) and carries planner units u (1 u = 100 m, path_manager.h:897), not metres. Marker scales (makeTube scale, makeChain 3*scale and 4*scale label height, 0.45 line width in makeTrajectoryRisk cpp:313) are in u too. The header comment block never states frame, units or that the frame is not configurable; the only evidence is the example printing frame=map and a private comment in path_manager.h.
findings.misreading_example: ROS users assume frame 'map' is metres (REP-103). A caller who feeds a metre-valued route to makeFrontEndPath, or passes scale=1.0 meaning 1 m for makeTrajectoryTube, gets a 100x wrong display. A caller in another frame cannot change "map" and silently gets messages in the wrong frame.
findings.reason: Names (makeFrontEndPath, scale) are fine once the contract sentence exists; renaming would not fix it. Add to the header block: 'All coordinates are planner units u, frame_id is fixed to "map"; makeTrajectoryClear uses "world"'. Parameter names in the declarations can cheaply become sphere_diameter_u etc. because positional callers are unaffected.

findings.issue: 'Tube' is a SPHERE_LIST of dense spheres (cpp:92-93 region and path_manager.h:733-737 comment), `scale` is the sphere diameter in u, trajectory sampling is a hard-coded 0.1 s plus the exact endpoint (cpp:103-123), `drone_id` is silently clamped with std::max(0, drone_id) (cpp:86) and also becomes the marker id and ns suffix, `ns_prefix` is a prefix not a namespace, and r,g,b,a are four positional floats after a double and a string. findings.issue: `Stamp` is not a stamp but a std::function<Time()> clock that every make*() calls once per marker (13 stamp() calls in the cpp; makeChain calls it per junction/label). Messages therefore get different stamps within one array when the callback is node->now() (path_manager.cpp:1876-1879). Error text and header call it a 'clock'. makeFrontEndPath alone takes a concrete Time under the same parameter name `stamp` (h:85), so the same variable cannot be passed to both.
findings.misreading_example: A caller writes `const viz::Stamp stamp = ...; viz::makeFrontEndPath(points, stamp)` (compile error) or, in the other direction, a slow/expensive callback (e.g. one that locks a clock service) is passed assuming it is called once and then costs O(markers) calls. Another caller assumes all markers of a MarkerArray share one header stamp.
findings.proposed_name: StampSource (only if the owner wants a rename; keep `using Stamp = StampSource;` for compatibility)
findings.reason: Rename candidate is cheap (real uses: path_manager.h:894, path_manager.cpp:1876, test 1, example 1, plus the 9 declarations in the header) but the confusion is mild and compile errors protect the type mismatch. Prefer documenting: 'invoked once per stamped marker; must be cheap and monotonic'. Also note the example itself shows the inconsistency (planning_visualization_example.cpp:8,13,19: stamp() for the path, stamp for the tube).

findings.symbol: make*() empty-input and clear semantics (makeChain, makePipeline, makeTrajectoryRisk, makeRiskProfile, makeRiskHeatmap, makeRiskField, makeDynamicObstacles, makeFrontEndPath vs makeTube)
findings.issue: The verb 'make' hides that most results are full-state REPLACEMENTS or CLEAR commands, and the rule differs per function: makeChain/makePipeline/makeRiskField/makeDynamicObstacles always put a DELETEALL first (cpp:138,233,795,1189 region), makeTrajectoryRisk returns action DELETE on empty/zoneless input (cpp:316-322), makeRiskProfile returns an empty Float64MultiArray (cpp:~488), makeRiskHeatmap returns a 1x1 all-NaN grid (cpp:583-596), makeFrontEndPath returns an empty Path, makeTube/makeTrajectoryTube return std::nullopt (no clear). The header summary says only 'Empty trajectories keep the original clear/no-tube behavior' (h:23).
findings.misreading_example: A caller who composes two makeChain/makeRiskField arrays on one topic (e.g. one per drone) loses the first because each starts with DELETEALL. A caller who passes an empty trajectory to makeRiskProfile and publishes the empty array expects 'nothing', but the altitude panel treats it as 'clear stale profile'.
findings.reason: Behaviour is deliberate (latched-topic atomic repaint, documented in path_manager.cpp:2020-2026 comment and the usage doc's last paragraph) and wire-compatible; renaming to makeXxxReplacement would be noise. A 10-line table in the header (function -> empty input result -> clears prior state?) removes the surprise.
findings.affected_callers: All 13 PathManager call sites; no external callers; test/planning_visualization_test.cpp:58-77,120-125 already pins the empty cases

findings.symbol: visualization::RiskSettings (mode, agl, step, slice_offset, contours, grounded, threshold, softness, heatmap_* fields)
findings.issue: Fields have no units and no mode applicability. `mode` is a free string whose valid set (heatmap | heatmap3d | volume | fixed_agl | fixed_msl) appears only in optimizer_params.yaml:178 and cpp:582,803-805,1052; unknown strings silently become the fixed_msl planar slice for makeRiskField (cpp:1047-1075) but an all-NaN stub for makeRiskHeatmap (cpp:583). `agl` is only the fixed_agl diagnostic height (yaml:197), `slice_offset` only for planar mode, `contours` only for volume mode, `step<=0` means automatic (h:51-52). `agl` vs `heatmap_agl_max` vs obstacle_clearance are three different AGL notions. findings.misreading_example: A caller sets settings.mode="slice" (reasonable guess) and gets a fixed_msl point cloud from makeRiskField and an empty heatmap; another sets settings.agl=0.15 believing metres (it is u, 15 m) or sets settings.agl for the heatmap modes where it is ignored.
findings.reason: The field names mirror the ROS parameters (risk_mask_viz_* in path_manager.cpp:1913-1925) and are mapped in one place; a rename would break that traceability for no gain. findings.symbol: RiskView callbacks (value, visibility, shadow_ceiling) and TerrainView callbacks (elevation, elevation_and_gradient)
findings.issue: Bare callback names with no units/frame in the declaration. `value` is the per-zone effective risk in [0,1] (not a generic 'value'), `shadow_ceiling` is an ABSOLUTE height in u of the line-of-sight horizon or a non-finite 'no shadow' value, z arguments are absolute (not AGL), terrain `elevation` returns float with NaN/-inf meaning unavailable (h:28 comment, but code also treats +inf as unavailable: cpp groundAt isfinite). The same 'terrain height at (x,y)' concept is exposed with three different conventions across the public API (see vocabulary_notes), and the evaluator's version signals unavailability by returning false, this one by NaN.
findings.misreading_example: A user reuses the evaluator's terrain lambda `[](double,double,double *h){*h=0;return true;}` for TerrainView (does not compile), or ports it to float(double,double) and returns 0 for 'unknown' instead of NaN, so the heatmap treats off-map cells as sea-level terrain. A caller supplies shadow_ceiling as AGL metres.
findings.reason: Names are consistent with PathManager's own riskZoneValue/riskVisibilityValue/riskShadowCeiling (path_manager.cpp:1889-1894) and the struct comment already says 'same canonical field as planning'. Cost of rename high (14+ test lines build lambdas), benefit low. Add unit/frame/unavailable-encoding comments and cross-reference the evaluator's provider convention.

findings.issue: A third obstacle type next to the public SphereObstacle/BoxObstacle/DynamicObstacle (planning_environment.h:32-42). Conventions are not stated in the header: for a sphere `size` must be the DIAMETER triple (2r,2r,2r) (cpp:1217-1221 'stored as (2r,2r,2r)'), while SphereObstacle uses `radius`; for a box `size` is the full extent and `center` is the box centre (cpp:1213-1216); `yaw` is radians about Z; `mesh_scale` is silently clamped with std::max(1.0, mesh_scale) (cpp:1232) so values <1 cannot shrink the mesh; it is also fed from the differently named catalog field `viz_scale` (path_manager.cpp:2410). makeDynamicObstacles additionally emits an invisible (alpha 0) CUBE 'dynamic_obstacles_geom' companion marker per obstacle that panels rely on (cpp:1243-1262).

findings.symbol: MissionPlanner::plan() as used in mission_planner_example.cpp (adoption side effect)
findings.issue: Overlaps another reviewer's area. The example calls planner.plan(mission) and prints result.trajectory_id. In the ROS backend plan() is compute + applyPlanningComputation (ros_planning_backend.cpp:213-217): it adopts the result into the backend's execution slot, mints a monotonically increasing trajectory_id and can revoke the previous trajectory. The non-adopting compute() exists only on RosPlanningBackend (ros_planning_backend.h:42), not on MissionPlanner. mission_planner.h:125-130 and the example header comment (:1-2) do not mention adoption; README.md:24-27 only says 'does not issue a vehicle execution command'.
findings.misreading_example: A user calls plan() twice with different candidate missions to compare them, expecting a pure function; the second call replaces the adopted execution slot and consumes ID 2, so anything holding the backend (FSM, executionManager) sees the new trajectory.
findings.reason: Keep the name: plan() is the right user-facing verb and the planner/backend split is documented in planning_computation_usage_ko.md. One sentence in mission_planner.h and the example comment ('adopts into the backend execution store and assigns trajectory_id; use RosPlanningBackend::compute for non-adopting candidates') is enough.
findings.affected_callers: MissionPlanner::plan() callers: mission_planner_example.cpp:55, test/mission_planner_test.cpp, docs planning_library_usage_ko.md

finding.proposed_name: publishFrontEndPath, publishTube, publishChain, publishPipeline, publishTrajectoryRisk, publishRiskProfile, publishRiskHeatmap, publishRiskField, publishDynamicObstacles (clearTrajectory keeps its verb)
finding.reason: One class, created in the current modularization, zero external callers and zero tests, 12 call sites in a single .cpp plus one doc sentence; the rename is mechanical and removes a real verb/side-effect ambiguity.
